A title heuristic with unmeasured recall: an appropriations act whose title lacks the pattern, or an appropriations division inside another bill, is NULL (money_bill_rule names the rule that fired). A simple or concurrent resolution (H. Res., S. Res., H. Con. Res., S. Con. Res.) is never a money bill, though a House special rule names the one it brings up, and `omnibus` is an appropriations omnibus only, not a statute named "Omnibus" (the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act).
columns.fiscal_year: Fiscal year the display title states, spelled FY plus the year: `fiscal year 2027`, the long title's `for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2027`, or an appropriations act's closing year (`... Appropriations Act, 2027`, `Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027`). Never read from short_title, which a reused vehicle takes from the act it replaced. NULL where the title states none.
columns.appropriations_subcommittee: Which of the twelve appropriations subcommittees the title names, under the statutory names: the House's National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs reads `State, Foreign Operations`. Read only where the regular-appropriations rule (or a manual override) classified the bill.
columns.short_title: The publisher's short title for the whole measure: the first titles[] entry whose titleType names a short title, which is the newest stage's because the publisher lists titles newest stage first, skipping the types that name only portions of the bill (an omnibus's divisions); NULL where the measure states no short title for the whole of it, which is ordinary.
columns.related_bills: Every relatedBills entry the publisher states, as a Native list, with each one's relationship details nested; this replaces BillTrax's hand-set related_bill_id with the publisher's own fact. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.related_bill_count: How many related bills the publisher states.

columns.citing_opinion_id: CourtListener opinion ID of the opinion that cites. Joins court_opinions.opinion_id.
columns.cited_opinion_id: CourtListener opinion ID of the opinion cited. Joins court_opinions.opinion_id.
columns.depth: Number of times the citing opinion cites the cited one.
columns.dump_date: The CourtListener bulk export the row was copied from (ISO date).
columns.source_sha256: SHA-256 of the CourtListener export file the row was read from (`sha256:` and 64 hex digits): the original, kept in the raw archive and the run's source evidence.

columns.citation_id: CourtListener citation ID. Primary key within one export.
columns.cluster_id: CourtListener decision-cluster ID the citation names; joins court_opinion_clusters.cluster_id.
columns.volume: Reporter volume as the publisher records it (a string; some volumes are years).
columns.reporter: Reporter abbreviation, such as `U.S.`, `F.3d` or `WL`, as the publisher records it.
columns.page: Starting page or equivalent locator in the reporter, as text.
columns.citation_type: Publisher citation type code: 1 federal reporter, 2 state, 3 state regional, 4 specialty, 5 early U.S. Supreme Court, 6 Lexis, 7 WestLaw, 8 vendor-neutral, 9 law journal.
columns.date_created: Timestamp the publisher created the citation record.
columns.date_modified: Timestamp the publisher last modified the citation record.
columns.dump_date: The CourtListener bulk export the row was copied from (ISO date).
columns.source_sha256: SHA-256 of the CourtListener export file the row was read from (`sha256:` and 64 hex digits): the original, kept in the raw archive and the run's source evidence.

columns.cl_docket_id: CourtListener docket id of a grouped row in `court_dockets`. Primary key.
columns.parent_cl_docket_id: The group's representative row: the member with the lowest PACER case id in its court's sequence, else the lowest numeric id (see the summary). Equal to cl_docket_id on the representative's own row. Not a main case the publisher marks; it marks none.
columns.confidence_tier: What the group's rows are: `per_defendant_dockets` (a criminal case's per-defendant dockets: the ids the representative was chosen from run consecutively with at most four missing, or a member carries CourtListener's defendant number) or `duplicate_records` (several records of one filing). Says nothing about refiling: a refiled case gets a new docket number, which this grouping cannot see.
columns.group_size: Number of published court_dockets rows in the same-case group.

columns.cl_docket_id: CourtListener docket id (e.g. `73613631`). Primary key / dedup key of a docket object, not of a case: one case can be several rows (`court_docket_groups`). Distinct from the regulations.gov `docket_id`.
columns.case_name: Short case name (e.g. `HENNEPIN COUNTY, MINNESOTA v. U.S. DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES`). Names the defendant agency as text, not as an identifier. For decisions in cases missing here, including appeals of agency orders, search `court_opinion_clusters.case_name`.
columns.case_name_full: Full case caption when available; often blank.
columns.court_id: CourtListener court identifier (e.g. `dcd` D.D.C., `cadc` D.C. Circuit, `akd` D. Alaska).
columns.court: Human-readable court name (e.g. `District Court, District of Columbia`).
columns.date_filed: Date the case was filed (ISO 8601 string). Sort key and incremental watermark.
columns.date_terminated: Date the case was terminated, if closed (ISO 8601 string). Null for pending cases.
columns.date_argued: Date of oral argument, if any (ISO 8601 string). Often null.
columns.nature_of_suit: Nature-of-suit label as CourtListener spells it. Every row came from the 899 (Administrative Procedure Act) selection, but the label varies: with or without the number (appellate dockets write 2899 or 3899), abbreviated as APA or Admin Proc Act, blank or NULL, and on a few rows another code. Filtering on one exact string misses most rows; you do not need this column to find APA suits.
columns.cause: Statutory cause of action as recorded in PACER (e.g. `05:551 Administrative Procedure Act`).
columns.jurisdiction_type: Basis of federal jurisdiction (e.g. `U.S. Government Defendant`).
columns.jury_demand: Jury demand recorded on the docket (e.g. `None`).
columns.assigned_to: Name of the judge assigned to the case.
columns.referred_to: Name of the magistrate/referral judge, if any. Often null.
columns.parties: Native list of party names on the docket (plaintiffs and defendants, including the defendant agency). `[]` when the publisher names none; NULL when the docket came from the bulk edition and its names have not been read yet. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.attorneys: Native list of attorney names appearing on the docket. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.firms: Native list of law-firm / legal-organization names appearing on the docket. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.pacer_case_id: PACER case id for the docket in its court's CM/ECF system, as CourtListener states it. Not always the court's own number for the case: CourtListener writes 10–15-digit values on some dockets (73 rows, mostly txwd and nysd, measured 2026-10-03) and keeps an older docket object's id when it reuses that object for a new case (`16` on three objects created 2020-12-22 for cases filed 2024 and 2025); some rows have none.
columns.case_type: Case-type code parsed from a district-court `docket_number` (`1:26-cv-02460` is `cv`, civil; also `cr` criminal, `mj` magistrate, `po` petty offense, `mc` miscellaneous). NULL when the number carries none, as appellate numbers do. The publisher codes non-civil dockets 899 too; they are kept, so filter on this for civil litigation.
columns.blocked: Whether the source marks the court docket blocked.
columns.date_blocked: Source-stated date when the docket was blocked.

columns.cluster_id: CourtListener opinion-cluster ID: this table's primary/dedup key, one per CourtListener record of a decision, not per decision. The publisher can hold several clusters for one decision, a Supreme Court slip opinion and its later U.S. Reports print above all, and later opinions cite either (Loper Bright: 9986254 and 10600041). Count decisions by `scdb_id`, the publisher's decision key, where it is set; it is unset on every Supreme Court cluster filed after 2019. Otherwise group by `cl_docket_id` and reporter citation (court_citations), a heuristic that misses a decision with no reporter citation yet. Join to court_opinions.cluster_id and court_citations.cluster_id; not an opinion_id.
columns.cl_docket_id: CourtListener docket ID, renamed from docket_id. Joins court_dockets.cl_docket_id only where both tables hold the same publisher docket object (an appellate case often has two: the court-website scraper's, named here, and RECAP's, held there), so match on the docket number when the id does not join; unrelated to regulations.gov docket_id.
columns.court_id: CourtListener court identifier from the docket map or search record; NULL when unresolved.
columns.court_jurisdiction: CourtListener jurisdiction code from the court reference lookup; NULL when unavailable.
columns.court_is_federal: `t` where CourtListener's jurisdiction code for the court starts with F (F appellate, FD district, FB bankruptcy, FBP bankruptcy appellate panel, FS special), `f` otherwise, as a string; NULL when the classification is unavailable. FS covers courts outside the circuit system, Article I courts and executive adjudicators among them (`cit`, `uscfc`, `cavc`, `bia`, `mspb`), so `t` does not mean an Article III court: filter `court_jurisdiction` for that.
columns.case_name: Source case caption; not a stable identity or affiliation link.
columns.case_name_short: Source short case caption, when supplied by bulk data.
columns.case_name_full: Source full case caption when supplied.
columns.date_filed: Source decision filing date; used by search catch-up, not an observation or correction date.
columns.date_filed_is_approximate: Source flag stating whether date_filed is approximate, stored as a string.
columns.judges: Source judge text; names are not normalized person identifiers.
columns.nature_of_suit: Source nature-of-suit text when supplied; this cluster table is not limited to the docket rollup's 899 query.
columns.precedential_status: CourtListener's source precedential-status value; this table does not independently assess legal authority.
columns.citation_count: The publisher's count of citing opinions at observation time, as a string: opinions, not decisions, and only decisions carrying a reporter citation are ever cited.
columns.scdb_id: Supreme Court Database identifier as supplied by CourtListener: the publisher's decision key for a Supreme Court decision where it is set. NULL on every Supreme Court cluster filed after 2019 (2026-06-30 export), whose decisions only the heuristic `cluster_id` names can group.
columns.scdb_decision_direction: Source Supreme Court Database decision-direction code; retained without interpretation.
columns.scdb_votes_majority: Source Supreme Court Database majority-vote count, stored as a string.
columns.scdb_votes_minority: Source Supreme Court Database minority-vote count, stored as a string.
columns.attorneys: Source attorney text; does not retain structured person identity. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.summary: Source summary text when supplied; not a generated SpicyRegs summary.
columns.other_dates: Source other-dates text, without date normalization.
columns.cross_reference: Source cross-reference text, without inferred identifier resolution.
columns.correction: Source correction text when supplied; not proof that later corrections have been acquired.
columns.blocked: Source blocked flag as a string; not a current access check.
columns.date_blocked: Source date of blocking when supplied.

columns.opinion_body_id: Stable identity of this opinion and captured body version; independent of extraction processing.
columns.opinion_id: Native CourtListener opinion ID selected for acquisition.
columns.cluster_id: Native opinion cluster ID from that same held opinion row.
columns.text_content: Derived PDF text when fingerprint and extraction checks succeed; null after a refusal.
columns.source_url: Literal download_url offered by the selected opinion.
columns.resolved_url: Final response URL observed by the provider.
columns.source_sha256: SHA-256 of complete captured PDF bytes.
columns.native_sha1: Body SHA-1 asserted by the selected native opinion row.
columns.actual_sha1: SHA-1 independently computed over captured bytes.
columns.pdf_extraction_results_json: URL, body SHA-256, status, page count and error for the selected attempt.
columns.parent_opinion_publication_json: Exact selected opinion family and its member metadata.
columns.sha1_matches: Whether the captured bytes match the native fingerprint, stored as text.
columns.parent_artifact_digest: Exact recorded court-opinions artifact used for this capture. A current opinion lookup is a separate check.
columns.parent_generation_id: Receipt generation of the recorded court-opinions parent, when declared. Null for older parents without native receipts.
columns.parent_member_sha256: SHA-256 of the exact recorded court-opinions member; never an identity inferred from a URL or native SHA-1 alone.
columns.parent_member_byte_size: Declared byte size of the recorded court-opinions member.

columns.opinion_id: CourtListener opinion ID. Primary key; joins court_citation_map and court_parentheticals opinion ids.
columns.cluster_id: CourtListener decision-cluster ID the opinion belongs to; joins court_opinion_clusters.cluster_id.
columns.opinion_type: Publisher opinion type code, such as `010combined`, `020lead`, `030concurrence` or `040dissent`.
columns.author_id: CourtListener judge ID of the author, when the publisher linked one.
columns.author_str: Author as the publisher's source text names them; not resolved to a person.
columns.joined_by_str: Judges joining the opinion, as the publisher's source text names them.
columns.page_count: Page count of the original document when known.
columns.sha1: Publisher's SHA-1 of the original document; not a SpicyRegs capture digest.
columns.download_url: Where the publisher obtained the original document, when recorded; no current accessibility claim. For court-website opinions the file name usually carries the lead docket number (a consolidated case lists two), the fallback key to court_dockets.docket_number.
columns.local_path: Path of the original document in CourtListener's storage, not a SpicyRegs file.

columns.date_created: Timestamp the publisher created the opinion record.
columns.date_modified: Timestamp the publisher last modified the opinion record.
columns.dump_date: The CourtListener bulk export the row was copied from (ISO date).
columns.source_sha256: SHA-256 of the CourtListener export file the row was read from (`sha256:` and 64 hex digits): the original, kept in the raw archive and the run's source evidence.

columns.parenthetical_id: CourtListener parenthetical ID. Primary key within one export.
columns.described_opinion_id: CourtListener opinion ID of the opinion the parenthetical summarizes. Joins court_opinions.opinion_id.
columns.describing_opinion_id: CourtListener opinion ID of the opinion that wrote the parenthetical. Joins court_opinions.opinion_id.
columns.text: The parenthetical as the describing opinion wrote it.
columns.score: Publisher's 0-to-1 estimate of how descriptive the text is.
columns.group_id: Publisher's group of parentheticals making the same point; NULL when ungrouped.
columns.dump_date: The CourtListener bulk export the row was copied from (ISO date).
columns.source_sha256: SHA-256 of the CourtListener export file the row was read from (`sha256:` and 64 hex digits): the original, kept in the raw archive and the run's source evidence.

columns.report_id: CRS report id (e.g. `R48641`, `IN12713`). Together with `update_date`, identifies one retained revision.
columns.title: Report title as returned by the list endpoint.
columns.status: Congress.gov's own status, `Active` or `Archived`, as stated; the list route does not define it, and an `Archived` report can carry a recent `published_date`.
columns.published_date: The publisher's `publishDate` for this retained report version, as the list route states it. Dates the version, not necessarily the first issue (R44997, first issued in 2017, carries 2026-04-29 at version 16). The list route gives no first-issue date.
columns.update_date: Source timestamp when the Congress.gov record was updated. Together with report_id, identifies one retained revision. It is separate from the discovery checkpoint and does not establish first publication.
columns.version: Version number of the report as returned by the list endpoint. Detail enrichment requires an explicitly stated matching version.
columns.summary: Complete summary from the matched report detail, including any publisher markup. See detail_fields for missing, null and empty states.
columns.authors: Native author entries in source order, preserving repeated and null entries. See detail_fields for the state of the source field.
columns.topics: Native topic entries in source order, preserving repeated and null entries. An explicit empty list remains empty.
columns.formats: Native format and URL entries in source order. A listed file is not evidence that its body was acquired.
columns.related_materials: Native report references in source order, preserving repeated and null entries. Source URL or url becomes url; numeric identifiers become text. Original spelling and types remain in captured detail.
columns.detail_state: Whether qualified detail is retained for this revision: not_requested or ok. A failed later attempt does not erase a previously qualified detail.
columns.detail_attempt_state: Outcome of the most recent detail attempt, separate from whether qualified detail is retained.
columns.detail_fields: One entry per supported source detail field, recording missing, null, empty or value. These states describe the qualified detail and its witness.
columns.detail_error: Reason for a failed detail attempt, when present. Previously qualified values may remain available with their original witness.

columns.bill_id: The bill both printings belong to.
columns.from_printing_id: Which acquisition path supplied the earlier printing.
columns.to_printing_id: Which acquisition path supplied the later printing.
columns.headline: One sentence naming the most important change.
columns.key_changes: The bullet points describing the most significant changes, as a Native list in the model's order. The prompt asks for at most five and nothing enforces it -- unlike bill_summaries.top_provisions, whose cap is checked before the row is stored -- because the ported answer schema states no maximum either, so a longer list is the model's answer and not a defect to hide. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.sections_added: Section headings that were added, as a Native list. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.sections_removed: Section headings that were removed, as a Native list. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.dollar_changes: Notable dollar-amount changes in prose, as a Native list. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.

columns.recent_30d: Documents the agency posted in the trailing 30 days.
columns.baseline: Prior-year monthly mean document count (months 2–13 back).

columns.docket_id: The docket's id; its API record is https://api.regulations.gov/v4/dockets/{docket_id}.
columns.category: The docket's status (labelled “Disposition”): Pending, Closed and others.
columns.display_properties: The agency's labels for this docket's fields: a Native list of {label, name, tooltip}; [] when none; json_column spelling. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.effective_date: Mostly the docket's close date (usually labelled “Docket Close Date”), a UTC instant.
columns.field1: An agency-defined field (“Related Docket's RIN”, “Related To”, …); see display_properties.
columns.field2: An agency-defined field (usually “Docket Status”); see display_properties.
columns.generic: An agency program code (“Docket Item Code”, “Location”, “Program Area”).
columns.keywords: The docket's keywords, in the publisher's order. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.legacy_id: The docket's id in a predecessor system.

columns.docket_id: Unique docket identifier (e.g. `EPA-HQ-OAR-2021-0317`). Primary key / dedup key.
columns.agency_code: Posting agency's short code (e.g. `EPA`, `FDA`, `ACF`). `lookup_agency` resolves it to Federal Register, eCFR and Federal Hierarchy organizations through RefSpec's REF-038 projection (vendored `reference/refspec/agency-projection.parquet`): measured 2026-10-30, 189 of 196 codes on 279,595 of 279,719 rows; `TRAIN`, `PCSCOTUS`, `USC`, `ERULE`, `EOA`, `BSC` and `GAPFAC` have no projection row.
columns.title: Human-readable docket title.
columns.modify_date: Timestamp the docket was last modified on regulations.gov (ISO 8601 string).
columns.abstract: Agency-written summary of the docket (regulations.gov `dkAbstract`). Often null.
columns.rin: Regulation Identifier Number tying the docket to the Unified Agenda. Often null.

columns.document_id: The document's id; its API record is https://api.regulations.gov/v4/documents/{document_id}.
columns.address1: The submitter's street address, first line, as stated.
columns.address2: The submitter's street address, second line, as stated.
columns.allow_late_comments: Whether the agency accepts comments after the period closes, as the publisher stated it on the record's latest version; the comment window's state comes from its dates.
columns.author_date: When the document was written (labelled “Author/ Document Date”), a UTC instant.
columns.authors: The document's authors, people or organizations, in the publisher's order; almost all on Supporting & Related Material. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.category: The submitter's sector category the agency assigns.
columns.cfr_part: The CFR parts the document affects, free text as stated.
columns.comment: The record's comment text as stated, markup included.
columns.display_properties: The agency's labels for this record's fields: a Native list of {label, name, tooltip}, name being the attribute it labels; json_column spelling. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.effective_date: When the action takes effect, a UTC instant.
columns.exhibit_location: Where a physical exhibit is held.
columns.field1: An agency-defined field; its meaning is the record's display_properties label (“Answer Date”, “XRIN”, “RTID”, …).
columns.field2: An agency-defined field; its meaning is the record's display_properties label (labelled “File Date”).
columns.fr_vol_num: The Federal Register volume or citation, free text as stated.
columns.gov_agency: The government body that submitted the document.
columns.gov_agency_type: That body's level: Federal, State, Local, Tribal, Regional, U.S. House of Representatives or U.S. Senate.
columns.implementation_date: The implementation or service date, a UTC instant.
columns.legacy_id: The record's id in a predecessor system (“Document Legacy ID”, “Legacy Exhibit Number”, …).
columns.media: How the document arrived: Electronic, Paper, … (spellings vary).
columns.omb_approval: An OMB control number, as stated.
columns.open_for_comment: Whether the document was open for comment, an observation as the publisher stated it on the record's latest version rather than a live status; the comment window's state comes from its dates.
columns.organization: The organization the author or submitter names.
columns.original_document_id: The id of the document this one derives from; sometimes the empty string.
columns.postmark_date: The postmark date (often labelled “Answer Date”), a UTC instant.
columns.receive_date: When the agency received the document, a UTC instant.
columns.restrict_reason: Why access is restricted, free text.
columns.restrict_reason_type: The restriction's kind: Copyrighted, Confidential Business Information, Personally Identifiable Information or Other.
columns.start_end_page: The Federal Register start and end pages, as stated.
columns.state_province_region: The submitter's state, province or region.
columns.subject: The subject line.
columns.submitter_rep: The name of the submitter's representative.
columns.subtype: The agency's subtype: Correspondence, Report, Decision and others.
columns.topics: The publisher's topics, in its order. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.within_comment_period: Whether the document arrived within the comment period, where given, as the publisher stated it on the record's latest version; the comment window's state comes from its dates.

columns.document_key: The citing document's own natural key in its family's spelling: the GovInfo `packageId` for a package, and one value per family as the table takes each one.
columns.document_kind: Which family the citing document belongs to, so one table serves all of them.
columns.cite_kind: What kind of thing is cited, by the rule that read it: `bill_number`, `public_law`, `statutes_at_large`, `usc_section`, `cfr_section`, `federal_register_cite`, `rin`, `gao_product_id`, `crs_report_id`, `docket_number`, `case_docket_number`, `us_reports_cite` or `committee_name`.
columns.target_key: The cited key in the hosted target's own spelling, which is part of this row's identity: `congress_bills.bill_id` for a bill, the joined `laws` identity for a law, a committee's `system_code`.  Where nothing settled it, the rule's canonical form of the printed text stands instead and `target_resolved` says so, because an unsettled key is still evidence and dropping it would lose what only the print holds.
columns.span_start: Character offset of the match in the document's normalized text, counted from zero.  Part of the identity: one document naming one bill forty times is forty rows, and the offset is what tells them apart.
columns.span_end: Character offset just past the match, so `text[span_start:span_end]` is `matched_text`.
columns.matched_text: The exact characters the rule matched, so a false positive is readable from the row without the document in hand.
columns.target_resolved: Whether `target_key` is the hosted target's own spelling.  `false` means the rule found the cite but nothing settled the key: a bill with no stated Congress, or a committee name no supplied roster reaches.  A shape check, not an existence check: a resolved key can name nothing the target table holds; join the target table to learn whether it is held.
columns.target_rule: How the key was reached. Bill routes distinguish inline_congress, congress_subheading, document_fallback, unstated and document_fallback_refused after the bill_number: prefix. A document fallback is context supplied by the caller, not proof of historical applicability. Other kinds use the rule name except `committee_name`, where it is the resolution route: `exact` and `roster_prefix` are lookups in the roster vocabulary, while `name_prefix` and `sibling_prefix` are inferences from the printed text of this one document.  A consumer wanting only roster lookups filters on this column rather than on `target_resolved`.
columns.stated_by_index: Whether a keyed index record for this document already states this target key -- the package MODS's own `<bill>`, `<law>` and `<USCode>` section elements and its authoring committee.  NULL where no index record was supplied.  This is the owner's do-not-recreate rule, carried per row: where it is `true` the row's value is the evidence span, not the key, and `WHERE stated_by_index IS NOT TRUE` selects the kinds that are genuinely new.
columns.body_version_id: Digest of the normalized text the offsets index into, and part of the identity.  A span means nothing without it -- a re-extraction that moved one character moves every offset after it -- and keying on it is what stops two extractions of the same document from colliding on one identity and silently merging.  The table is append-only per digest: a superseded extraction's rows are not retired, and a consumer filters to the digest `house_activity_reports.text_sha256` states for that document.
columns.target_table: The namespace the target key belongs to, as the rule names it (`congress_bills`, `gao products (product id as GAO prints it)`): what the key identifies, not whether a host holds a table of it.

columns.document_id: Unique document identifier. Primary key / dedup key.
columns.docket_id: Parent docket this document belongs to. Foreign key to `dockets.docket_id`.
columns.agency_code: Posting agency's short code. `lookup_agency` resolves it through RefSpec's REF-038 projection: measured 2026-10-30, 307 of 316 codes on 2,003,671 of 2,004,396 rows; the rest (`USC`, `BSC`, `TRAIN`, `PCSCOTUS`, `GAPFAC`, `ERULE`, `ARCTICGAS`, `PRES`, `EOA`) have no projection row.
columns.title: Document title.
columns.posted_date: Date the document was posted publicly (ISO 8601 string).
columns.modify_date: Timestamp the document was last modified (ISO 8601 string).
columns.comment_start_date: Literal Regulations.gov commentStartDate. See data_quality for the source-specific calendar conversion; this field does not establish submission purpose. NULL means no value was retained.
columns.comment_end_date: Literal Regulations.gov commentEndDate as Regulations.gov states it now, which can reflect a later extension rather than the notice's own date: when a later notice extends the period, Regulations.gov can rewrite the original notice's date too (FS-2025-0001-223869, FR 2026-16965, reads 2026-10-07T03:59:59Z, the extension FR 2026-18648 set, while the Register's comments_close_on for 2026-16965 is 2026-09-21). For the date a notice printed, read federal_register.comments_close_on by fr_doc_num. Convert offset-bearing instants to America/New_York for calendar searches; date-only values and the source's bare T00:00:00Z convention keep their printed day (see data_quality). Neither purpose nor the controlling/current deadline follows from this field; inspect filing instructions and later notices. NULL does not mean no deadline.
columns.attachments: Native list of the main document's fileFormats renditions: `[{url, format, size}]`. This compatibility field does not contain separately listed attachment resources. Null when no main renditions were retained. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.attachment_records: Native list of the main document's fileFormats renditions: `[{url, format, size}]`. This compatibility field does not contain separately listed attachment resources. Null when no main renditions were retained. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.fr_doc_num: Federal Register document number, when the document was published in the FR. Often null.
columns.withdrawn: Whether regulations.gov flags the posting withdrawn, as the string `"true"`/`"false"`. Often null. A withdrawn posting is still held here; the rulemaking tables read it as no evidence (see `proceedings`).
columns.reason_withdrawn: Agency-supplied reason for withdrawal, when withdrawn: usually that it was posted to the wrong docket, a duplicate, moved or replaced. Often null.
columns.additional_rins: Native list of additional Regulation Identifier Numbers beyond the docket's primary RIN. Often null. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.text_content: Plain text extracted from the document's PDF attachment(s) by the PDF text-extraction step. Null until that step has run; see `text_extraction_status`.
columns.publisher_status: What Regulations.gov last said of the document when the daily reconcile step checked its docket: `listed` (the docket's document listing names it, or, where the listing does not, its own record still answers) or `removed` (the listing omits it and its own record answers 404 or 410). NULL where the step has never checked it: it checks only dockets with a document posted or modified in the past week, so NULL does not mean the publisher still serves it. A removed document stays in this table (see data_quality).
columns.removed_observed_at: When the reconcile step first found the document removed, as a UTC ISO 8601 instant; NULL unless `publisher_status` is `removed`.
columns.file_url: URL of the document's primary downloadable rendition. Retained for backward compatibility; see `attachments` for the full list. Often null.
columns.text_extraction_status: Aggregate PDF outcome: `ok` means at least one PDF supplied text, even if another failed; otherwise `error`, `encrypted`, or `empty` (no extractable text) in that order. Null before an attempt. See `pdf_extraction_results_json` for each file.
columns.pdf_extraction_results_json: Ordered JSON array from the latest PDF attempt: `{url, source_sha256, status, page_count, error}` per distinct selected URL. SHA-256 identifies observed bytes; no-bytes fetch failures have null digest/page count and a generic error. Null when no PDF attempt is recorded. Describes that attempt, not the provenance of older text retained after a failed overwrite.

columns.id_submission: ECFS submission id (e.g. `26109947027`). Primary key / dedup key. The filing's page on fcc.gov (`https://www.fcc.gov/ecfs/filing/<id_submission>`, the former `filing_url` column) is kept in the filing's receipt, not in this table: ask `read_receipt_fields` for the field `filing_url`.
columns.proceedings: Source-listed FCC proceedings with their names and identifiers; repeated occurrences remain distinct. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.submission_type: ECFS submission type description, e.g. `COMMENT`, `REPLY TO COMMENTS`, `NOTICE OF EXPARTE`.
columns.express_comment: Publisher express-comment flag, normalized to BOOLEAN. NULL means the publisher omitted the flag or supplied null; retained native evidence distinguishes those states. The flag alone does not establish document availability.
columns.date_received: Timestamp ECFS records the filing as received (ISO 8601 string). Incremental cursor and sort key.
columns.date_submission: Timestamp the filer submitted the filing (ISO 8601 string).
columns.date_disseminated: Timestamp the filing was disseminated (made public) by ECFS (ISO 8601 string).
columns.exparte_or_late_filed: `Y` if the filing is ex-parte or late-filed, else `N`.
columns.filers: Native list of filer names (individuals or organizations) on the filing. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.authors: Native list of author names on the filing, when distinct from the filers. Often empty. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.lawfirms: Native list of law-firm names on the filing. Often empty. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.bureaus: Native list of FCC bureau names the filing was routed to. Often empty. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.text_data: The filing's inline text — for express comments this is the full comment text. Null for document-only filings.
columns.total_page_count: Total page count across the filing's attached documents, as a numeric string.
columns.documents: Native list of attached documents as `{filename, src}` objects, where `src` is the fcc.gov download URL. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.generation_id: Selected main filing generation. Binds retained result observations to this filing version; it is not the original attempt time.
columns.extraction_results: Latest retained extraction results in source order: URL, status, body digest, page count, error and matching offered document positions. Null means no result was recorded; an empty list means the retained result list was empty. Repeated offers keep every position. Capture custody and extracted-text access remain unverified. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.

columns.name: Proceeding (docket) number, e.g. `17-108` or `23-320`. Primary key / dedup key, and the join key to the `name` of each entry in `fcc_filings.proceedings`.
columns.id_proceeding: ECFS numeric identifier, reused across some docket names in retained data (301759 appears with both 17-108 and 87-432). Native filing-to-proceeding joins require name AND id_proceeding; the numeric ID alone is not globally unique. The table's primary key remains name.
columns.description: Proceeding title/subject (ECFS `description_display`, falling back to `description`), e.g. `Restoring Internet Freedom`. There is no program or topic field, and titles often leave the program out: Universal Service dockets include 13-184 (`Modernizing the E-rate Program for Schools and Libraries.`) and 02-60 (`In the Matter of Rural Health Care Support Mechanism`), neither of which says universal service, and high-cost programs such as the Rural Digital Opportunity Fund (19-126) and the 5G Fund (20-32) use their own names. Search titles together with bureau_code (WC, or CC for older dockets) and known docket numbers, and find related dockets by the proceedings filings name alongside an anchor docket in fcc_filings.proceeding_names_json (for Universal Service, the umbrella docket 96-45 and 10-90). A title search gives a floor, not a complete list.
columns.bureau_code: Code of the FCC bureau that owns the proceeding (e.g. `WC`).
columns.bureau_name: Name of the FCC bureau that owns the proceeding (e.g. `Wireline Competition Bureau`).
columns.rulemaking_or_docket: ECFS `flag_rulemaking_or_docket`: `R` for rulemakings (RM- numbers), `D` for dockets.
columns.filing_status: ECFS filing-window status for the proceeding (e.g. `OPENALL`): how filings are accepted, not whether the proceeding is open. Many closed proceedings still read `OPENALL`; see date_closed for the record-level closure convention.
columns.date_created: Timestamp the proceeding was created in ECFS (ISO 8601 string). Sort key.
columns.date_closed: ECFS-recorded closure timestamp. NULL or a future date can be used only as a record-level open convention; placeholders include 2099-12-31T23:59:59.999Z and 2100-01-31T05:00:00.000Z. Neither this convention nor a recorded closure establishes current legal effect, filing acceptance or an active comment period. Check filing_status and the specific notice's comment/reply instructions separately.
columns.filed_by: ECFS account that created the proceeding. An internal FCC username; occasionally useful for spotting bureau conventions.
columns.date_nprm: ECFS `date_nprm`: date of the proceeding's Notice of Proposed Rulemaking as ECFS records it, an ISO 8601 string with the publisher's UTC offset as written (96-82: `1996-04-01T00:00:00.000-05:00`). NULL when ECFS records none; 6,023 of 21,705 dockets carry one (retained walk 2026-10-08).
columns.date_reporting_and_order: ECFS `date_reporting_and_order`: date of the Report and Order as ECFS records it, an ISO 8601 string with the publisher's UTC offset as written (96-82: `1996-10-18T00:00:00.000-04:00`). NULL when ECFS records none; 5,290 of 21,705 dockets carry one (retained walk 2026-10-08).
columns.rule_section: ECFS `rule_section`: the CFR part or section the proceeding concerns, as typed by FCC staff (96-82: `PART 80 AND 87`; 96-96: `73.202(B)`). Free text, not a normalized citation. Leading and trailing whitespace is stripped and a blank value is NULL (owner decision 2026-10-31): ECFS writes an empty string or a single space where it has none and pads some values (` Part 76`); the receipt's `raw_record` keeps the value as ECFS wrote it. 11,259 of 21,705 dockets carry text, 16 of them stripped (retained walk 2026-10-08).

columns.record_id: Deterministic key for this mapped source observation within its table and generation; repeated captures remain distinct from a single economic event.
columns.identity_version: Version of the source-observation identity rule; it does not select a current or canonical record.
columns.mapping_version: Named, versioned source-to-field mapping used for this observation.
columns.mapping_status: Whether this source observation mapped fully, partially, or received an explicit nondata/refusal disposition; inspect the reason alongside NULL values.
columns.collection_id: Exact retained collection label. Join fec_collections in the selected source generation; the label alone is not a globally unique source identity.
columns.source_record_id: Native source-observation key within collection_id. Resolve with the source generation, exact locator and source digest, not this value alone.
columns.source_sha256: SHA-256 of the original source witness bytes; distinct from the typed table's publication digest.
columns.source_locator_json: Exact source row or subrecord coordinates, including available member, ordinal, byte span and field-definition references. Resolve in the pinned source generation.
columns.source_authority: Authority assigned to the selected source, preserving official FEC, unofficial originals and third-party research distinctions.
columns.selection_evidence_sha256: Digest of the retained selection evidence used to authorize this mapper's source scope; not a financial inclusion decision.
columns.source_representation_role: Selected source role such as snapshot, insertion or deletion. Amount signs and ordinary amendment flags do not establish correction applicability.
columns.correction_operation: Source-supported correction operation, when applicable; a positive amount in a deletion stream is not a new receipt or an inferred refund.
columns.correction_applicability_status: Whether the captured correction can be applied to an evidenced base and target population; unresolved applicability prevents a qualified current total.
columns.current_record_status: Explicit current-selection limitation or decision. Capture order and a mapped value alone do not establish the current record.
columns.filing_key: Nullable authority- and namespace-qualified filing-version key. Several retained observations can share it; group proven filing identity before joining. It does not by itself say whether the row's filing is held: where this table has a filing association view, that view decides it for each row (its `target_record_id` is this `record_id`; read its `association_status` and `filing_key`). `<table>_filing_associations` matches the filing's header record and `<table>_native_filing_associations` the FEC file number; `list_sources` names the views that exist.
columns.filing_link_status: Always `unresolved` in this table, with `filing_key` NULL beside it: both are set when the row is mapped, before any filing is looked up, so neither says whether the row's filing is held. Where this table has a filing association view, that view decides it for each row (its `target_record_id` is this `record_id`; read its `association_status` and `filing_key`): `<table>_filing_associations` matches the filing's header record and `<table>_native_filing_associations` the FEC file number. `list_sources` names the views that exist.
columns.currency: Currency explicitly assigned by the source-specific mapping; agency measure units are stated separately.
columns.amount_kind: Source-specific meaning of amount, such as a reported receipt, payment, balance or aggregate. It is not an aggregation permission.
columns.source_namespace: Namespace identifying the native layout or identifier system. Similar numbers or field names across namespaces are not equivalent.
columns.form_type: Literal filing form or record-type code from the source layout; does not prove submission conformance.
columns.reporting_committee_id: Literal FEC ID of the reporting committee where that source field identifies a committee. It does not by itself identify the sender or recipient of money.
columns.back_reference_transaction_id: Source-stated transaction back-reference. Resolve only within the evidenced filing and schedule scope; no automatic parent match.
columns.account_name: Account name as reported for the source transfer or activity record.
columns.activity_event_name: Source-stated activity/event name associated with this account transfer.
columns.event_type: Source-defined event or activity type, interpreted within this table and source namespace.
columns.source_amendment_code: Literal native amendment code; it does not establish replacement scope from the retained filing layout.
columns.transaction_id: Literal transaction identifier within its source filing/layout scope; not a globally unique transaction or economic-event key.
columns.financial_grain: Explicit financial row meaning selected for this layout, separating reported activity, balances, allocations and other observations.
columns.source_cycle: Election cycle established by the selected source evidence. Distinct from transaction year, candidate election year and agency fiscal year.
columns.transferred_amount: Exact decimal for the reported transfer between accounts. Signs are preserved; use the corresponding status and source-specific financial policy before adding observations.
columns.total_amount: Exact decimal for the whole reported payment or allocation total. Signs are preserved; use the corresponding status and source-specific financial policy before adding observations.
columns.transaction_date: Date parsed from the transaction date reported by the source. NULL requires the source value and conversion status; capture time is not substituted.
columns.definition_set_id: Key of the pinned source layout in fec_filing_definitions. Join its definition evidence for exact workbook cells; the layout does not validate the submission.
columns.filing_header_record_id: Source-record key of the actual file header. Resolve with collection_id and filing_header_locator_json in the source generation.
columns.filing_header_locator_json: Exact native coordinates of the file-header witness, separate from the financial row's own locator.
columns.voter_registration_amount: Exact decimal for reported voter-registration activity. Signs are preserved; use the corresponding status and source-specific financial policy before adding observations.
columns.voter_id_amount: Exact decimal for reported voter-identification activity. Signs are preserved; use the corresponding status and source-specific financial policy before adding observations.
columns.gotv_amount: Exact decimal for reported get-out-the-vote activity. Signs are preserved; use the corresponding status and source-specific financial policy before adding observations.
columns.generic_campaign_amount: Exact decimal for reported generic campaign activity. Signs are preserved; use the corresponding status and source-specific financial policy before adding observations.
columns.filing_association_status: The maintained association rule result. Resolved means a qualified filing key; unresolved reasons and not_evaluated never imply an edge or a current filing.
columns.filing_association_policy: Version of the maintained filing association rule used for this decision.
columns.filing_association_source_generation_pin: Exact selected source generation used for the filing association decision.
columns.filing_association_target_generation_pin: Exact separately selected filing-metadata generation for an external target. Null for a target in this same dataset generation (self); use the target scope to distinguish these cases.

columns.collection_id: Exact retained collection label. Join fec_collections in the selected source generation; the label alone is not a globally unique source identity.
columns.source_record_id: Native source-observation key within collection_id. Resolve with the source generation, exact locator and source digest, not this value alone.
columns.source_sha256: SHA-256 of the original source witness bytes; distinct from the typed table's publication digest.
columns.source_locator_json: Exact source row or subrecord coordinates, including available member, ordinal, byte span and field-definition references. Resolve in the pinned source generation.
columns.source_authority: Authority assigned to the selected source, preserving official FEC, unofficial originals and third-party research distinctions.
columns.selection_evidence_sha256: Digest of the retained selection evidence used to authorize this mapper's source scope; not a financial inclusion decision.
columns.source_representation_role: Selected source role such as snapshot, insertion or deletion. Amount signs and ordinary amendment flags do not establish correction applicability.
columns.correction_operation: Source-supported correction operation, when applicable; a positive amount in a deletion stream is not a new receipt or an inferred refund.
columns.correction_applicability_status: Whether the captured correction can be applied to an evidenced base and target population; unresolved applicability prevents a qualified current total.
columns.current_record_status: Explicit current-selection limitation or decision. Capture order and a mapped value alone do not establish the current record.
columns.filing_key: Nullable authority- and namespace-qualified filing-version key. Several retained observations can share it; group proven filing identity before joining. It does not by itself say whether the row's filing is held: where this table has a filing association view, that view decides it for each row (its `target_record_id` is this `record_id`; read its `association_status` and `filing_key`). `<table>_filing_associations` matches the filing's header record and `<table>_native_filing_associations` the FEC file number; `list_sources` names the views that exist.
columns.filing_link_status: Always `unresolved` in this table, with `filing_key` NULL beside it: both are set when the row is mapped, before any filing is looked up, so neither says whether the row's filing is held. Where this table has a filing association view, that view decides it for each row (its `target_record_id` is this `record_id`; read its `association_status` and `filing_key`): `<table>_filing_associations` matches the filing's header record and `<table>_native_filing_associations` the FEC file number. `list_sources` names the views that exist.

columns.source_representation_role: Selected source role such as snapshot, insertion or deletion. Amount signs and ordinary amendment flags do not establish correction applicability.
columns.current_record_status: Explicit current-selection limitation or decision. Capture order and a mapped value alone do not establish the current record.
columns.source_namespace: Namespace identifying the native layout or identifier system. Similar numbers or field names across namespaces are not equivalent.
columns.source_pointer: Exact pointer within the provider-owned native record to the mapped value or metadata object.
columns.filing_link_status: The stating filing's own `filing_link_status`, copied from `fec_filings` onto each link it states: `native_file_number` where that filing states its FEC file number, `unresolved_no_file_number` where it does not. It says nothing about the referenced filing; see `target_resolution_status`.
columns.target_resolution_status: Not a resolution result: set when the link is mapped, before any filing is looked up, as `native_reference_unresolved` on every link that states a file number and `unresolved_no_file_number` on the rest. columns.reference_status: Source-presence and interpretation state of the directed filing reference.
columns.source_cycle: Election cycle established by the selected source evidence. Distinct from transaction year, candidate election year and agency fiscal year.

columns.query_completeness: Whether complete traversal of the stated source query was established. A retained page or rejected response is not a completed query.
columns.matter_type: Legal source family such as advisory opinion, enforcement, administrative fine, dispute resolution, rulemaking or audit.
columns.source_namespace: Namespace identifying the native layout or identifier system. Similar numbers or field names across namespaces are not equivalent.
columns.native_matter_id: Literal case identifier within its legal source namespace; similar numbers across matter types do not identify the same case.
columns.native_document_id: Literal document identifier in its native matter/document namespace.
columns.title: Source title or explicitly labeled mapper title; consult title_basis or title_status when present.
columns.description: Literal source description or narrative associated with this observation.
columns.status: Legal status stated by the source at this observation, without selecting a current state across captures.
columns.source_url: Source-provided absolute URL, or navigation URL resolved from a source-provided relative FEC path. Supported legacy matter routes are rewritten only after exact matter-type and identifier checks. Absolute URLs remain unchanged; a missing URL is not invented. It does not assert current availability or body retrieval. The original URL remains in source evidence.
columns.committee_id: Literal FEC committee identifier as reported in this observation. Use cycle and source scope for historical joins.
columns.candidate_id: Literal FEC candidate identifier when the source reports one. Syntax checks do not prove identity resolution or a target match.
columns.audit_id: Literal source audit identifier; it does not replace the namespaced matter identity.
columns.currency: Currency explicitly assigned by the source-specific mapping; agency measure units are stated separately.
columns.reported_cycle: Cycle exactly as reported in a native field; kept separate from the selection's source_cycle.
columns.is_pending: Source-reported pending flag for this legal matter; not an independently determined legal status.
columns.is_published: Source-reported publication flag for this legal matter; not proof that a document body was acquired.
columns.challenge_outcome: Literal administrative challenge outcome reported by the source.
columns.civil_penalty_payment_status: Literal source-reported civil-penalty payment status; distinct from the parsing status of this field.
columns.report_type: Source-reported report classification, interpreted within its namespace rather than as a universal period code.
columns.mur_type: Literal Matter Under Review type stated by the source.
columns.committee_description: Source-provided description of the committee associated with this legal matter.
columns.committee_designation: Literal designation of the committee referenced by this legal matter.
columns.committee_type: Single-letter committee type code (e.g. `P` presidential, `H` House, `S` Senate, `N`/`Q`/`O` PAC variants).
columns.rm_id: Source rulemaking identifier, preserved exactly as text; distinct from native_matter_id and rm_number.
columns.rm_number: Source rulemaking number including its literal prefix; distinct from rm_id and native_matter_id.
columns.report_year: Year reported for the filing/report, preserved independently of cycle and transaction date.
columns.is_open_for_comment: Source-reported comment-window flag; it is not recalculated using the current clock.
columns.final_determination_amount: Exact decimal for the source-stated final determination in the legal matter. Signs are preserved; use the corresponding status and source-specific financial policy before adding observations.
columns.payment_amount: Exact decimal for the payment amount stated in the legal matter observation. Signs are preserved; use the corresponding status and source-specific financial policy before adding observations.
columns.reason_to_believe_fine_amount: Exact decimal for the source-stated reason-to-believe fine amount. Signs are preserved; use the corresponding status and source-specific financial policy before adding observations.
columns.treasury_referral_amount: Exact decimal for the amount stated for referral to Treasury. Signs are preserved; use the corresponding status and source-specific financial policy before adding observations.
columns.election_cycles: Election cycles stated for the legal matter; original order and repetitions are preserved. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.ao_citations: Advisory opinions cited by this legal matter, retaining source citation attributes. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.aos_cited_by: Advisory opinions that cite this matter, retaining the source direction. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.regulatory_citations: Source-listed regulatory citations; no applicability determination is implied. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.statutory_citations: Source-listed statutory citations; no applicability determination is implied. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.citations: Source-listed legal citations, grouped by citation kind with literal text and URLs. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.subject: Publisher subject hierarchy with source identifiers and ordered child links. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.subjects: Publisher subject identifiers in source order, preserving repeated entries. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.non_monetary_terms: Nonmonetary terms stated in the legal matter. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.non_monetary_terms_respondents: Respondents associated with the source-stated nonmonetary terms. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.

columns.record_id: Deterministic key for this mapped source observation within its table and generation; repeated captures remain distinct from a single economic event.
columns.identity_version: Version of the source-observation identity rule; it does not select a current or canonical record.
columns.mapping_version: Named, versioned source-to-field mapping used for this observation.
columns.mapping_status: Whether this source observation mapped fully, partially, or received an explicit nondata/refusal disposition; inspect the reason alongside NULL values.
columns.collection_id: Exact retained collection label. Join fec_collections in the selected source generation; the label alone is not a globally unique source identity.
columns.source_record_id: Native source-observation key within collection_id. Resolve with the source generation, exact locator and source digest, not this value alone.
columns.source_sha256: SHA-256 of the original source witness bytes; distinct from the typed table's publication digest.
columns.source_locator_json: Exact source row or subrecord coordinates, including available member, ordinal, byte span and field-definition references. Resolve in the pinned source generation.
columns.source_pointer: Exact pointer within the provider-owned native record to the mapped value or metadata object.
columns.source_authority: Authority assigned to the selected source, preserving official FEC, unofficial originals and third-party research distinctions.
columns.selection_evidence_sha256: Digest of the retained selection evidence used to authorize this mapper's source scope; not a financial inclusion decision.

columns.matter_record_id: Exact fec_legal_matters.record_id observation supporting this child event, party, document or finding.

columns.role: Party role exactly as stated in the legal matter or supporting document; read role_status and identity_resolution_status before forming a relationship.
columns.reported_name: Person or organization name exactly as reported in this legal party assertion.
columns.native_entity_id: Literal party identifier where the source reports one; names are not converted into IDs.
columns.entity_namespace: Native identifier namespace of the reported party/entity.
columns.entity_type: Source entity-type code or namespace-specific type expected for the reported party.
columns.document_record_id: Exact typed legal-document observation cited by this party or other source assertion.

columns.filing_key: Nullable authority- and namespace-qualified filing-version key. Several retained observations can share it; group proven filing identity before joining. It does not by itself say whether the row's filing is held: where this table has a filing association view, that view decides it for each row (its `target_record_id` is this `record_id`; read its `association_status` and `filing_key`). `<table>_filing_associations` matches the filing's header record and `<table>_native_filing_associations` the FEC file number; `list_sources` names the views that exist.

columns.transaction_id: Literal transaction identifier within its source filing/layout scope; not a globally unique transaction or economic-event key.
columns.back_reference_transaction_id: Source-stated transaction back-reference. Resolve only within the evidenced filing and schedule scope; no automatic parent match.

columns.guarantor_organization: The loan guarantor's organization name as reported, without resolving it to a corporate identity.
columns.guarantor_committee_id: The loan guarantor's literal committee ID where reported; not an inferred committee relationship.
columns.guarantor_first_name: The loan guarantor's reported given name.
columns.guarantor_middle_name: The loan guarantor's reported middle name.
columns.guarantor_prefix: The loan guarantor's reported name prefix.
columns.guarantor_suffix: The loan guarantor's reported name suffix.
columns.guarantor_street1: The loan guarantor's first reported street-address line.

columns.guarantor_state: The loan guarantor's reported state value.
columns.guarantor_zip: The loan guarantor's reported postal code, preserving leading zeroes.
columns.employer: Employer name reported for the contributor or other named person; not an inferred organization identity.
columns.occupation: Occupation reported by the source for the named person.
columns.source_cycle: Election cycle established by the selected source evidence. Distinct from transaction year, candidate election year and agency fiscal year.
columns.guaranteed_amount: Exact decimal for the amount guaranteed by this source-named guarantor. Signs are preserved; use the corresponding status and source-specific financial policy before adding observations.
columns.definition_set_id: Key of the pinned source layout in fec_filing_definitions. Join its definition evidence for exact workbook cells; the layout does not validate the submission.
columns.filing_header_record_id: Source-record key of the actual file header. Resolve with collection_id and filing_header_locator_json in the source generation.

columns.filing_association_status: The maintained association rule result. Resolved means a qualified filing key; unresolved reasons and not_evaluated never imply an edge or a current filing.
columns.filing_association_policy: Version of the maintained filing association rule used for this decision.
columns.filing_association_source_generation_pin: Exact selected source generation used for the filing association decision.
columns.filing_association_target_generation_pin: Exact separately selected filing-metadata generation for an external target. Null for a target in this same dataset generation (self); use the target scope to distinguish these cases.
columns.filing_association_record_id: Identity of the admitted association witness; null when source context or a singular header witness is unavailable.
columns.filing_association_referenced_key: Qualified filing key stated by a supported source reference, before checking retained targets. Null when the reference cannot be qualified.
columns.filing_association_target_generation_sco: Whether the filing target belongs to this same dataset generation (self) or a separately pinned generation (external). Self targets have no external generation pin; the scope alone does not establish a resolved match.
columns.filing_association_target_count: Number of observed filing-metadata witnesses for the qualified reference. Null means the target population is not established; no witness is selected as latest.
columns.filing_association_target_record_ids: Every matching filing observation identifier in the selected target population, preserving repeated witnesses. Null means the population is not established. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.

columns.org_tp: Publisher financial-summary field ORG_TP; its literal value qualifies the reported summary.
columns.prim_election: Publisher financial-summary field PRIM_ELECTION; its literal value qualifies the reported summary.
columns.pty_cd: Publisher financial-summary field PTY_CD; its literal value qualifies the reported summary.
columns.run_election: Publisher financial-summary field RUN_ELECTION; its literal value qualifies the reported summary.
columns.receipt_date: Publisher financial-summary field Receipt_Date; its literal value qualifies the reported summary.
columns.report_type: Publisher financial-summary field Report_Type; its literal value qualifies the reported summary.
columns.spec_election: Publisher financial-summary field SPEC_ELECTION; its literal value qualifies the reported summary.
columns.sponsor_name: Publisher financial-summary field Sponsor_Name; its literal value qualifies the reported summary.
columns.tres_nm: Publisher financial-summary field TRES_NM; its literal value qualifies the reported summary.
columns.measures: Source-specific monetary measures as a list of structs: native_field, raw_value, exact DECIMAL value, value_status and unit. Unnest with record_id; never add parent summaries to their itemized details. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.filing_association_status: The maintained association rule result. Resolved means a qualified filing key; unresolved reasons and not_evaluated never imply an edge or a current filing.
columns.filing_association_policy: Version of the maintained filing association rule used for this decision.
columns.filing_association_source_generation_pin: Exact selected source generation used for the filing association decision.
columns.filing_association_target_generation_pin: Exact separately selected filing-metadata generation for an external target. Null for a target in this same dataset generation (self); use the target scope to distinguish these cases.
columns.filing_association_record_id: Identity of the admitted association witness; null when source context or a singular header witness is unavailable.
columns.filing_association_referenced_key: Qualified filing key stated by a supported source reference, before checking retained targets. Null when the reference cannot be qualified.
columns.filing_association_target_generation_sco: Whether the filing target belongs to this same dataset generation (self) or a separately pinned generation (external). Self targets have no external generation pin; the scope alone does not establish a resolved match.
columns.filing_association_target_count: Number of observed filing-metadata witnesses for the qualified reference. Null means the target population is not established; no witness is selected as latest.
columns.filing_association_target_record_ids: Every matching filing observation identifier in the selected target population, preserving repeated witnesses. Null means the population is not established. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.

columns.record_id: Deterministic key from the retained original's SHA-256 and this row's native position in it (fec-original-tables/1); repeated captures remain distinct from a single economic event.
columns.title: Source title or explicitly labeled mapper title; consult title_basis or title_status when present.
columns.link: Literal RSS item link retained from the source feed.
columns.guid: Source RSS item GUID, scoped to the feed; not promoted to a filing number or a globally resolved identity.
columns.reported_filer_id: Literal identifier labelled CommitteeId in the source feed; candidate filings can carry candidate identifiers under this label.
columns.committee_id: OpenFEC committee identifier (e.g. `C00684373`). Committee join key; this feed row is identified separately. Joins `fec_committee_history.committee_id` for per-cycle names and the connected organization.
columns.candidate_id: Literal candidate identifier reported by API metadata or a verified named bulk field such as CAND_ID. Blanks and aggregate codes remain literal; an ID-shaped aggregate value does not establish a person. Names are not converted to identifiers.
columns.filing_id: Source-reported sub_id of a filing metadata row when present; not an inferred original-file number. Amendment/current-record meaning remains in native metadata.
columns.form_type: Literal filing form or record-type code from the source layout; does not prove submission conformance.
columns.report_type: Source-reported report classification, interpreted within its namespace rather than as a universal period code.
columns.coverage_start_date: Build-parsed CoverageFrom date; requires exact MM/DD/YYYY spelling and a valid calendar date.
columns.coverage_end_date: Build-parsed CoverageThrough date; requires exact MM/DD/YYYY spelling and a valid calendar date.
columns.published_at: Build-parsed feed publication instant from an exact four-digit-year GMT timestamp; invalid input remains null with parsing status.
columns.mapping_version: Named, versioned rule that built this row from its retained original.
columns.collection_id: Capture collection that retained the original, the lowest id when one original was captured in several parts. Join fec_collections in the selected source generation; it is not the part that held this row.
columns.source_authority: Authority assigned to the selected source, preserving official FEC, unofficial originals and third-party research distinctions.
columns.source_url: Captured source URL for this observation; it does not assert current availability or body retrieval.
columns.source_sha256: SHA-256 of the retained original this row was read from; with the row's native position it is the row's own witness.
columns.current_record_status: Explicit current-selection limitation or decision. Capture order and a mapped value alone do not establish the current record.
columns.source_label_status: Whether the feed's CommitteeId label contains a committee identifier, a candidate identifier, a missing value or an unsupported spelling.
columns.parsing_status: Interpretation of source parsing: distinguishes reported/parsed values, missing/null/empty source states and unsupported spellings. A NULL typed value alone does not identify the cause.
columns.filing_link_status: Source feed assertion only; the value does not qualify a filing match or establish the target exists.

columns.record_id: Deterministic key from the retained original's SHA-256 and this row's native position in it (fec-original-tables/1); repeated captures remain distinct from a single economic event.
columns.meeting_type: Meeting classification explicitly stated by the retained HTML table.
columns.title_raw: Meeting title exactly as retained in the source row, including cancellation language.
columns.reported_status: Status explicitly stated in the source, including cancellation where the meeting table reports it.
columns.dates: Literal date cells and available date interpretations for the meeting row; multiple dates remain separate. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.links: Source links with their labels and exact native locations; metadata does not imply body retrieval. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.date_kind: Whether the meeting dates represent one date, separately listed dates, or the two endpoints of a range.
columns.mapping_version: Named, versioned rule that built this row from its retained original.
columns.collection_id: Capture collection that retained the original, the lowest id when one original was captured in several parts. Join fec_collections in the selected source generation; it is not the part that held this row.
columns.source_authority: Authority assigned to the selected source, preserving official FEC, unofficial originals and third-party research distinctions.
columns.source_url: Captured source URL for this observation; it does not assert current availability or body retrieval.
columns.source_sha256: SHA-256 of the retained original this row was read from; with the row's native position it is the row's own witness.
columns.date_status: Conversion state for the reported transaction/context date; distinguishes exact values, source NULL/empty and invalid or unsupported spelling.

columns.record_id: Deterministic key from the retained original's SHA-256 and this row's native position in it (fec-original-tables/1); repeated captures remain distinct from a single economic event.
columns.page_type: Supported type of retained source documentation page, such as a form page or statutory filing reference.
columns.title: Source title or explicitly labeled mapper title; consult title_basis or title_status when present.
columns.text: Build-extracted body text of the page. Original page text and context remain at the evidence reference.
columns.content_scope: Scope of retained page content; text, headings and links are source documentation rather than inferred transactions.
columns.links: Source links with their labels and exact native locations; metadata does not imply body retrieval. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.mapping_version: Named, versioned rule that built this row from its retained original.
columns.collection_id: Capture collection that retained the original, the lowest id when one original was captured in several parts. Join fec_collections in the selected source generation; it is not the part that held this row.
columns.source_authority: Authority assigned to the selected source, preserving official FEC, unofficial originals and third-party research distinctions.
columns.source_url: Captured source URL for this observation; it does not assert current availability or body retrieval.
columns.source_sha256: SHA-256 of the retained original this row was read from; with the row's native position it is the row's own witness.
columns.content_status: Page body disposition; always body_extracted, because only pages whose body was extracted are published. Failed, empty and unsupported pages are refused and listed by reason in the conversion proof's refused_originals.

columns.document_number: The Register's document number, spelled as it serves it (`2017-07442`, unpadded before 2013).
columns.title: The document's title.
columns.abstract: The agency's abstract of the document; often NULL.
columns.document_type: The Register's category as the API states it: `Rule`, `Proposed Rule`, `Notice`, `Presidential Document`, and on older records `Uncategorized Document`, `Correction` (none after 2008-08-08) and `Sunshine Act Document`; NULL on a few records. Since 2008 a correction, an effective-date delay or a confirmation of a rule is itself typed `Rule` and shares the rule's RIN, docket and title; subtype is NULL on recent records, so tell them apart by `action`.
columns.publication_date: The date the document was published, canonical YYYY-MM-DD.
columns.effective_on: The `effective_on` date the Federal Register API states for the document. On a rule it is usually the effective date; the API also states one on some proposed rules and notices (a comment-period extension can carry the original proposal's date), so a date here does not by itself show that anything took effect. NULL where the API states none, as on most notices.
columns.comments_close_on: The public comment deadline, for a document that opens a comment period; often NULL.
columns.signing_date: The date a presidential document was signed; NULL for other documents.
columns.agencies: The issuing agencies as the Register's agency objects, a Native list. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.agency_slugs: The issuing agencies' Register slugs, comma-separated; NULL when none. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.docket_ids: The docket labels the document states, a Native list, as printed (many are agency numbers). Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.regulation_id_numbers: The Regulation Identifier Numbers the API lists, a Native list. `[]` on a large share of Rule documents every year, an API limit: some of those state a RIN in the printed text, and some print it inside docket_ids. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.cfr_references: The CFR citations the document affects, a Native list of `{title, part, chapter, citation_url}`. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.topics: The Register's CFR index terms for the document (`topics`), a Native list; `[]` when it lists none. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.subtype: The Register's subtype when the API sets it; NULL on recent records, so it does not separate a correction from its rule (`action` does).
columns.executive_order_number: The executive order number, for a presidential executive order; NULL otherwise.
