columns.modify_date: Always NULL: the Register's API states no update instant.
columns.rin: The host's derived first RIN of `regulation_id_numbers`; NULL when it states none.
columns.regulations_dot_gov_docket_id: The regulations.gov docket the Register states for this document; NULL where it states none, even where it states a document: a docket is never read off the front of a document id.
columns.regulations_dot_gov_document_id: The regulations.gov document the Register states for this document; NULL where it states none.
columns.regulations_dot_gov_comments_count: Regulations.gov's comment count for that document as the Register relayed it at regulations_dot_gov_checked_at. The Register stops checking soon after the comment period closes, so the count is as of that check. It can be far higher than the comments regulations.gov posts (IRS-2024-0010-0001: 384,423 against 12 posted, 2026-10-03): a different fact from the posted comment rows this service holds. NULL where the Register states no count.
columns.regulations_dot_gov_checked_at: When the Register last checked regulations.gov for this document, as it states it (UTC); NULL where it has not checked.
columns.action: The document's action line as the API states it (`Final rule.`, `Final rule; correction.`, `Proposed rule; extension of comment period.`); NULL where it states none, as on many older records. It tells a rule from its later correction, delay or confirmation, which share the rule's type, RIN, docket and title.
columns.correction_of: For one of the Register's own editorial corrections (numbered like `C1-2012-1234`), the API address of the document it corrects; NULL otherwise. An agency's correction published as a rule carries no such link; its `action` names it a correction.
columns.corrections: The API addresses of the corrections the Register links to this document (its own editorial corrections), a Native list; `[]` where it links none. NULL on a row not read since the field was first requested (2026-10-03). Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.significant: Whether the document was deemed significant under Executive Order 12866, as the API states it: `true` or `false`; NULL where the API states neither, which is common, so NULL does not mean `false`.
columns.president_json: The Register's literal presidential attribution object, with identifier and name; no signer inference. NULL means unrequested/missing; JSON null and an empty object remain distinct.
columns.disposition_notes: Literal Register disposition prose; NULL if missing/null, empty text if stated empty.
columns.executive_order_notes: Literal Register executive-order history prose, including spelling and line breaks; not an independently established current legal effect.
columns.regulations_dot_gov_agency_id: Agency identifier stated by the linked Regulations.gov document metadata.
columns.regulations_dot_gov_title: Title stated by the linked Regulations.gov document metadata.
columns.regulations_dot_gov_regulation_id_number: Regulation identifier number stated by the linked Regulations.gov metadata; no inferred docket or rule match.
columns.regulations_dot_gov_supporting_documents: Supporting-document count stated by Regulations.gov for the linked document.

Supporting document identifiers and titles listed by Regulations.gov, preserving source order and repetition. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.regulations_dot_gov_regulatory_plan_titl: Regulatory-plan title stated in the linked Regulations.gov metadata.
columns.body_html_url: The document's full-text HTML body; the XML body the Register also serves carries no boilerplate.
columns.source_sha256: SHA-256 of the retained Federal Register API page this row was last read from, as the run's source-evidence journal spells it (`sha256:<hex>`); the page is `source-evidence/blobs/sha256/<hex>`. NULL on a row no run has read since the column was added (2026-11). It is a pointer, not part of the record: the scheduled run re-reads the last 120 days, so it changes every night on every row in that window (about 8,700) whether or not the record changed, and a comparison of two generations must leave it out. Where one run reads a document on two pages it names the first.
columns.regulations_dot_gov_info_json: The Register's own statement of the regulations.gov docket and document it matched this document to (the API's `regulations_dot_gov_info`), a JSON object exactly as stated: `{}` where the Register states nothing, the time of its check alone where it checked and found nothing, otherwise any of the docket, the document, the comment count, the supporting documents and their titles. NULL on a row not read since the field was first requested (2026-10-03).

columns.docket_id: Docket identifier. One row per docket.
columns.title: Docket title (from `dockets`).
columns.modify_date: Docket last-modified timestamp; the table is sorted by this descending.
columns.comment_count: Posted comments on the docket, summed from `comments_index`, less those on a posting Regulations.gov removed (`documents.publisher_status`). 0 when none. These are posted comment records, not comments received: an agency posts one record for a mass-mail campaign that can stand for thousands of submissions (EPA-HQ-OW-2022-0114 has 1,629 posted records for about 122,200 comments EPA received). To estimate submissions received, sum `comments.duplicate_comments` as its description says; this table does not carry it.
columns.comment_end_date: Latest comment-period end date across the docket's documents, less postings Regulations.gov removed. Null when unknown.
columns.date_created: Earliest document `posted_date` on the docket, less postings Regulations.gov removed, used as a creation date. Null when unknown.

columns.bill_id: The bill both printings belong to.
columns.from_printing_id: Which acquisition path supplied the earlier printing.
columns.to_printing_id: Which acquisition path supplied the later printing.
columns.seq: The section_diff_items row this pairing came from.
columns.amount_index: Position of this pairing within that section's word alignment.
columns.label: The section heading, which BillTrax left empty in every row it wrote.
columns.from_amount: The figure on the earlier side, or NULL where the alignment found none.
columns.to_amount: The figure on the later side, or NULL where the alignment found none.
columns.delta: to_amount minus from_amount, or NULL when either side is absent.
columns.pairing_claim: What this row claims: that the two figures sit at the same place in a word-level alignment. It does not claim they are the same account.

columns.docket_id: The docket as the statement gives it: a printed label verbatim from `docket_ids` (`Docket No. FAA-2007-29334`, an agency docket number, a `FRL-` number), or the Register's regulations.gov docket id.
columns.docket_source_ordinal: Zero-based position of a printed label in the original docket array, before null/blank elements are filtered; NULL on a row the regulations.gov link alone carries. With document_number and publication_date it identifies a printed occurrence.
columns.document_number: Literal Federal Register document number. Join to `federal_register` on both this value and `publication_date`; a number can name distinct dated records.
columns.title: FR document title.
columns.subtype: FR subtype where the Federal Register supplies one, e.g. `Final Rule`, `Interim Final Rule`.
columns.publication_date: Date the document published in the Federal Register; required with `document_number` for the FR record join.
columns.effective_on: Date the rule takes effect, when the document carries one.
columns.comments_close_on: Comment period close date, when the document carries one.
columns.agency_slugs: Federal Register agency slugs for the issuing agencies. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.docket_ids: The full original docket-ID array, retained so consumers can see the other IDs this FR document links to. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.regulation_id_numbers: RINs (Native list) claimed by the FR document — the RIN-side join key for a rulemaking. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.executive_order_number: Executive order number, for presidential documents.
columns.link_source: Which of the Register's statements carries the pair: `printed` (the document's printed docket labels), `regulations_dot_gov_info` (the Register's regulations.gov link, read from `regulations_dot_gov_docket_id` alone, never off a document id) or `both`, where a printed label is that docket id or SpicyDocs' normalizer reads it from the label. Every printed occurrence that carries the pair reads `both`, and the link then adds no row. The current builder writes one of these labels; retained historical rows without a label keep NULL.
columns.normalized_docket_candidates: Owner-normalizer candidate interpretations of the docket value; an empty array means no supported interpretation, not absence of a docket. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.

columns.decision_number: The decision's number as GAO's listing spells it, suffixes and all (`B-424129.2`, `B-423916.2,B-423916.3`, `B-235577.2-O.M.`, a docket `2020-02`). With `url`, the key.
columns.b_numbers: Native list of the decision's B-numbers: the ones its page's File line states where the page was read, else the ones in `decision_number`, split on commas and semicolons. GAO's listing cuts a few long lists, ending them `et al` or where its number field is full, and a fragment it cut mid-number is left out; b_numbers_truncated says where the list here is still the cut one. `[]` for a docket- or P-numbered decision. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.decision_type: GAO's label for the page as its listing states it: `Bid Protest Decision`, `Appropriations Decision`, `Legal Other Decision` and the like. A label, not a check: GAO also labels a few reports and letters `Bid Protest Decision` (B-423717, B-401197).
columns.title: The decision's heading as GAO's listing states it: the protester or the question decided. GAO double-escapes some headings, so a few keep `—`, `—` or `&` literally.
columns.topics: Native list of GAO's headings the decision was listed under, in listed order. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.url: The decision's gao.gov page, as the listing links it (percent-encoded where GAO encodes it). With `decision_number`, the key.
columns.released_date: The listing's Publicly Released date (its Published date where it states no release), as an ISO date: when GAO released the decision, not when it decided it (B-424477: decided 2026-08-07, released 2026-08-28). A count by fiscal year counts releases.
columns.decided_date: The day GAO decided the decision, from the Date line of its page's caption, as an ISO date; NULL where no page was read or the page prints no caption (a letter, a report, a decision GAO posts only as a PDF). GAO releases a decision after deciding it, often days later (B-424477: decided 2026-08-07, released 2026-08-28), so a count by decided_date and one by released_date differ.
columns.decision_status: GAO's outcome sentence for the decision as its listing states it, word for word with HTML whitespace collapsed (`We deny the protest.`); NULL where the listing states none.
columns.outcome: The outcome decision_status states, read by a closed table of GAO's exact sentences: `sustained`, `sustained_in_part`, `denied`, `dismissed`, `denied_in_part_dismissed_in_part`, or `request` where the sentence decides only a request (reconsideration, costs, reimbursement, dismissal); a sentence deciding the protest and a request reads the protest's outcome. NULL where no sentence is stated or the table does not read it (an advisory opinion, an appropriations opinion, a wording GAO wrote after the table was made): never a guess.
columns.b_numbers_truncated: `true` where GAO's listing cut the decision's numbers -- the list ends `et al` or in a separator, or fills the listing's number field (64 characters for decisions released 2009-2011, 252 from 2012) -- and no decision page has completed it, so b_numbers holds only what the listing names; `false` otherwise.
columns.listing_page: The first Month in Review or Annual Index page that listed the decision, as requested.
columns.source: The route that supplied the row: `gao_listing` (GAO's own Month in Review and Annual Index).

columns.recommendation_id: The key, rule `gao-recommendation-key/1`: a digest of the lowercased publication number, the kind, the number GAO states and the agency; where the text states no number, of the lowercased publication number, the agency and the text, whitespace runs folded and case folded.
columns.report_id: The publication number lowercased: the GAO product id `gao_reports` is keyed on.
columns.publication_number: The publication number exactly as GAO spells it, such as `GAO-26-108061`.
columns.publication_title: The publication's title as the export states it, a line break GAO left in it included.
columns.publication_date: The date GAO issued the publication, as an ISO date.
columns.director_name: The GAO director or directors the export names as the publication's contact, several joined by commas as GAO writes them, so a comma can also be part of one name (as in a suffix); NULL where it names none.
columns.agency: The agency the recommendation is made to, as GAO's addressee label spells it, with no parent department (U.S. Coast Guard is not nested under DHS); a generic label (`Office of the Director`, `Office of the Under Secretary`, `Other`) names different agencies on different publications, so read publication_title beside it. A recommendation made to several agencies is one row for each.
columns.recommendation: The recommendation's text in full, the number GAO states at its end included.
columns.recommendation_kind: Which of GAO's numbered series the text's closing tag names: `recommendation` to an agency, or `matter` for Congress to consider; NULL where the text states no number.
columns.recommendation_number: The number GAO states for it within its publication and kind, as GAO writes it; NULL where it states none.
columns.status: GAO's status for it as last listed: `Open` or `Open--Partially Addressed`.
columns.priority: Whether GAO designates it a priority recommendation, as last listed: `true` or `false`.
columns.comments: GAO's comments on the agency's progress as last listed, untrimmed; NULL where it states none.
columns.topics: The topic the export files it under, as last listed; NULL where it states none.
columns.first_seen: The date the status-as-of stamp states on the first export read that listed it: when this table first saw it open, not when GAO made it.
columns.last_seen: The date the status-as-of stamp states on the latest export read that listed it.
columns.listed_open: Whether the latest export read lists it under this key. `false` says only that it is no longer listed: GAO closing it is the usual cause, but an edit to its number, text or agency, or a defective export, reads the same.
columns.status_as_of: The export's own status-as-of stamp, verbatim, from the latest export that listed it; GAO labels it EST year round, though it is Eastern local time. Text in GAO's spelling (`Sep 30, 2026 at 1:18 PM EST`), not sortable: last_seen carries the same stamp's date in ISO form, so order and filter by it.

columns.report_id: GAO product id as gao.gov's product URL spells it (e.g. `gao-26-107974`, `t-rced-94-121`), lowercased. Primary key / dedup key. A GovInfo package id maps to that spelling (`GAOREPORTS-GAO-HEHS-00-73` is `hehs-00-73`, `GAOREPORTS-RCED-AIMD-94-221FS` is `rcedaimd-94-221fs`); a few keep GovInfo's spelling where the package id cannot recover gao.gov's.
columns.title: Product title as the route states it; on a listing row, the teaser's label and heading joined as `label: heading`, which is how the feed titles the same products. The Month in Review cuts a long heading at about 200 characters and ends it `...`; where GAO's major-rule listing states that heading whole, the title is whole. A `gao_major_rule_listing` or `gao_major_rule_index` row's is `Federal Agency Major Rule Report: ` and the heading GAO's listing or the report's product page states, or the heading alone on the AIMD- and GGD- products. A few GovInfo titles are GovInfo's placeholder `GAO Report from` and the number. Where our own routes leave it NULL, it may come from the CetiAlphaFive/gao R package (GPL-3.0-or-later, commit 6f61230), which fills only empty cells. GAO double-escapes some headings, so a few listing titles keep `—`, `—` or `&` literally, as GAO's page displays them; apply `html.unescape` when matching.
columns.report_type: GAO product type. The feed tags no finer type, so a feed or upstream-copied row is `Report`; a GovInfo or listing row is `Testimony` for a `T-` number or a number ending in `T`, else `Report`; NULL on a report added by explicit repair.
columns.published_date: Publication date as an ISO date string (e.g. `2026-07-17`): the feed's `pubDate` (upstream's feed for a copied row), GovInfo's `dateIssued`, the listing's "Publicly Released" date (its "Published" date where it states no release), GAO's issue date on a `gao_major_rule_listing` or `gao_major_rule_index` row (those listings state no release date), or the day a repaired product's page states. Sort key.
columns.abstract: The product summary: the feed's (GAO's `What GAO Found` / `Why GAO Did This Study` narrative), or a GovInfo row's MODS `abstract` with whitespace runs collapsed; NULL where neither states one, and on repair and listing rows. Where our own routes leave it NULL, it may come from the CetiAlphaFive/gao R package (GPL-3.0-or-later, commit 6f61230), which fills only empty cells.
columns.agencies: Reserved Native list of agencies the product covers. The RSS feed carries no structured agency tags, so this is `[]` pending a future enrichment source; NULL on repair, GovInfo (MODS names no agency) and listing rows. Where our own routes leave it NULL, it may come from the CetiAlphaFive/gao R package (GPL-3.0-or-later, commit 6f61230), which fills only empty cells. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.topics: Native list of topics. A GovInfo row's is its MODS `subject/topic` terms in the record's order, GAO's own index terms, program names and places, kept as stated (a long name can arrive split in two); NULL where the MODS states none or is unread. A listing row's is GAO's own topic headings the product was listed under, as GAO spells them and in listed order; a `gao_major_rule_listing` or `gao_major_rule_index` row's is NULL, since those listings state no topic. The RSS feed carries no topic tags, so a feed or upstream-copied row is `[]`; NULL on repair rows. Where our own routes leave it NULL, it may come from the CetiAlphaFive/gao R package (GPL-3.0-or-later, commit 6f61230), which fills only empty cells. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.url: The product's page on the route that supplied the row: the gao.gov product page for feed, upstream-copied, repair and every listing's rows, GovInfo's details page (composed from the package id) for GovInfo rows.
columns.source: The route that supplied the row: `gao_rss` (the daily feed), `upstream_copy` (copied once from upstream spicy-regs' published table), `gao_repair` (an explicit single-report repair), `govinfo` (GovInfo's GAOREPORTS listing), `gao_listing` (GAO's own Month in Review and Annual Index), `gao_major_rule_listing` (GAO's Congressional Review Act listing, "Reports on Major Rules"), `gao_major_rule_index` (GAO's index of 2000-12-15 of its 1996-2000 major-rule reports, and each report's product page) or `gao_r_package` (copied once from the CetiAlphaFive/gao R package by Jack T. Rametta, GPL-3.0-or-later).
columns.product_type: The publisher's product type, finer than `report_type`, which keeps its values. A GovInfo row's is its MODS type (e.g. `Letter Report`, `Correspondence`, `Testimony`, `Fact Sheet`, `Other Written Product`). A listing row has one only where GAO's teaser shows a finer type in place of a subject (`Federal Agency Major Rule Report`, on every major-rule report; `Correspondence`; `Other Written Product`); NULL where it shows a subject or only `Report`/`Testimony`. A report GAO's major-rule listings state is `Federal Agency Major Rule Report` on their word, whatever route holds its row: every `gao_major_rule_listing` and `gao_major_rule_index` row but the AIMD- and GGD- products that listing also states (NULL), and the few GovInfo rows those listings name, GAO-01-1024R among them though it reports on no rule (GAO lists it so; owner decision 2026-10-04). NULL on other routes and on unread GovInfo rows.
columns.report_number: The report number as the route prints it, the form other documents cite and users search for: a GovInfo row's MODS (e.g. `GAO-08-919R`, `RCED/AIMD-94-221FS`, `GAO/HEHS-00-73`) or the product number on GAO's listing page (e.g. `GAO-26-108426`, `OGC-96-9` for a major-rule report of 1996 to 2000, or `B-331093` for one from April 2017 on). The listing fills it on any row it lists whose number is NULL, whatever route supplied the row, and never replaces one. NULL on other feed, upstream-copied and repair rows, and on GovInfo rows whose MODS is unread. Where our own routes leave it NULL, it may come from the CetiAlphaFive/gao R package (GPL-3.0-or-later, commit 6f61230), which fills only empty cells.
columns.requester_type: Why GAO did the work, as the R package states it: `congressional_request`, `testimony`, `correspondence`, `cg_initiated` (the Comptroller General's own initiative) or `statutory_mandate`. NULL where the package states none, and on reports issued after its copy (2026-09-26) until a GAO product-page reader fills them.
columns.requester_committees: Native list of the requesting congressional committees, as the R package extracted them from the report (e.g. `Committee on Armed Services (Senate)`). NULL where it states none, and on reports issued after its copy. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.requester_members: Native list of the requesting members of Congress, as the R package extracted them from the report's text, with its OCR errors kept (e.g. `Charles H. Percy (Senate)`). NULL where it states none, and on reports issued after its copy. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.recommendation_count: How many recommendations the product makes (0 for none): the rows of "Recommendations for Executive Action" on the report's GAO product page where a page read has set it, else the R package's count. BIGINT. NULL on reports the package does not list and no page read has reached.
columns.matters_for_congress_count: How many matters for congressional consideration the product raises (0 for none): the rows of "Matter for Congressional Consideration" on the report's GAO product page where a page read has set it, else the R package's count. BIGINT. NULL on reports the package does not list and no page read has reached.
columns.page_count: The report's page count: the pages GAO's product page states for the file it labels Full Report where a page read has set it, else the R package's. BIGINT. NULL where neither states one.
columns.subject_terms: Native list of GAO's subject index terms for the product (e.g. `Cost control`, `Financial management`), finer than `topics`: the terms the report's GAO product page lists, as GAO spells them and in page order, where a page read has set it, else the R package's. GAO retags products, so the two can differ. NULL where neither states any. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.major_rule_agency: The agency that issued the rule a Federal Agency Major Rule Report is on, as the report's letter prints it in its opening sentence (e.g. `Department of Health and Human Services, Health Care Financing Administration (HCFA)`): one string in GAO's wording, abbreviations kept, the agencies of a joint rule in one clause and not split. It is not an agency key, and GAO spells one agency several ways. NULL on a row that is not a major-rule report, on one whose letter has not been read, and where the letter states no such clause.
columns.major_rule_rins: Native list of every Regulation Identifier Number the letter of a Federal Agency Major Rule Report states for the rule or rules the report is on, each as `NNNN-LLNN` (e.g. `2040-AB75`), in the letter's order. The join key to `unified_agenda.rin` and to the entries of `federal_register.regulation_id_numbers`. The list is not paired with `major_rule_fr_citations`: entry k of one is not the RIN of entry k of the other, and a report on two rules often states one RIN for both, so take a rule's RIN beside its citation from `federal_register`. NULL on a row that is not a major-rule report or whose letter has not been read, and where the letter states none in that form: it names a docket, an FCC number or a ZRIN instead, or GAO mistyped it. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.major_rule_fr_citations: Native list of the Federal Register citation of each rule a Federal Agency Major Rule Report is on, as its letter states it, each as `{volume}-{page}` (`66-6976` for 66 Fed. Reg. 6976), in the letter's order: one for most reports, several where a report is on several rules or on a rule published as several documents. Each joins `federal_register` on `volume` and `start_page` (`split_part(c, '-', 1) = volume AND split_part(c, '-', 2) = start_page`); a few letters cite the page before the document starts or a page inside it. A correction, a delay or an earlier rule the letter cites beside its rule is left out. Not paired with `major_rule_rins`. NULL on a row that is not a major-rule report or whose letter has not been read, and where the letter states no citation: the rule was not published in the Federal Register, or the letter's opening cites none. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.citation_product_id: Uppercase report number, falling back to the product-page ID only when the number is NULL. Blank numbers stay blank. This is a citation lookup key; report_id remains the record identity.

columns.package_id: The CHRG package the hearing was printed as, spelled exactly as `hearing_transcripts.package_id` is, which is this table's document key.
columns.congress: The numbered Congress, from the package id's own grammar.
columns.chamber: The chamber, from the package id's document-type code rather than from its first letter, the same rule `hearing_transcripts.chamber` uses.
columns.committee_system_code: The `authorityId` of the first `congCommittee` the package MODS names, already keyed the way `committees.system_code` is.  Half the join key a bill-side confirmation needs, and half the identity check an agenda row passed before it was written.
columns.held_date: The day the hearing was held, where the package MODS states one distinct `heldDate`; NULL where it states none or several (a compiled volume, whose dates are held_dates).  Not the day its transcript was issued.  The other half of the confirmation join key.
columns.event_id: The committee-meeting event id this link was reached through, so an agenda row joins `committee_meetings` and its own transcript row.  NULL on a cover row whose caller read no hearing detail: the MODS itself never states one.
columns.bill_id: `congress_bills.bill_id` for the measure, in the publisher's own type and number.  Part of the identity.
columns.link_id: Which rule in `interpretation/hearing_bill_links.py` stated this pair, from a sealed additions-only vocabulary: `mods_cover` (the package MODS's own cover list) and `docs_house_br` (the House Committee Repository's agenda) are implemented; `daily_digest_entry`, `congress_related_items` and `front_matter_designator` are measured, named and not yet filled.  Part of the identity, because two sources naming one pair is the evidence and collapsing them would delete it; additions-only because this value is published and a rename rewrites rows already out.
columns.relation: What the row asserts, from the sealed vocabulary `held_on` and `noticed`.  `mods_cover` rows are `held_on`, confirmed 19 of 20 by the bill's own action list; `docs_house_br` rows are `noticed`, because an agenda states intent and an agenda-only bill is confirmed 1 of 18, contradicted 1 and unverifiable 16.
columns.evidence_text: The exact string the rule read, so a wrong row is readable without the record in hand: the MODS `context` marker on a cover row, and the `BILLS-118HR188ih.pdf` file name, the `legis-num` or the `description` on an agenda row.
columns.held_dates: Every nonempty `heldDate` the package MODS states, as a Native list in document order with repetitions kept; `[]` where it states none.  A compiled volume states several, and which bill was heard on which day is not stated, so no bill is paired with a date.  NULL on a row not re-read since the column was added (`mods_cover` 002). Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.last_modified: The parent hearing package's publisher modification timestamp. Joins the exact dated transcript revision; neither held_date nor link_rule_version supplies this source coordinate.

columns.package_id: The GovInfo package id; last_modified identifies its retained package revision.
columns.collection: The GovInfo collection the package belongs to (CRPT, CHRG).
columns.congress: The numbered Congress, parsed from the package id's own grammar.
columns.hearing_type: The hearing's document-type code (hhrg, shrg, jhrg).
columns.jacket_number: The hearing's printing jacket number, leading zeros kept because it is opaque.
columns.chamber: The chamber, from the package id's document-type code rather than from its first letter.
columns.title: The package title as the keyed summary states it.
columns.date_issued: The date GovInfo issued the package; for CHRG packages this is the (first) held date: the summary's dateIssued equals the MODS's first heldDate on 185 of 185 published transcripts (2026-10-03), and the meeting's date on 117 of 117 matched to committee_meetings.  held_date states it from the MODS itself.
columns.last_modified: The publisher's package addition/update timestamp, including metadata-only updates. Together with package_id it identifies a retained revision; it is not first publication or a promise that every text change has a unique timestamp.
columns.body_version_id: Digest of the extracted text, so a re-extraction that changed nothing is visible as such.
columns.event_id: The committee-meeting event id the Congress.gov hearing record names as its associatedMeeting, which committee_meetings.event_id joins on; NULL where the hearing names none or was not looked up.
columns.witnesses: Every witness the package's GovInfo MODS states, as a Native list of its `<witness>` strings verbatim in document order -- name, position and organization as GPO wrote them, unsplit, because the record joins them in one string and spells them differently by chamber.  NULL where the MODS states none, never `[]`: MODS has no element for an empty witness list, so its silence is absence.  The Congress.gov meeting record lists no Senate witness at all, while the MODS lists them for 63 of 85 published Senate transcripts (2026-10-03). Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.committee_system_codes: The committees the package's GovInfo MODS names as holding the hearing: each `congCommittee` `authorityId`, the system code committees.system_code and committee_meetings.committee_system_code key on (`hswm00`), lower-cased the way they key it, once each in the order the MODS first states it, as a Native list. Read from the record and then each of its granules, because a hearing published as several states its committee only there (15 of 185 published transcripts, 2026-10-03); a joint hearing names two (3 of 185). `[]` where the MODS names none (1 of 185); NULL on a row not read since the column was added. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.held_date: The day the hearing was held, as the package's MODS states it in `<heldDate>`; NULL where the MODS states none.  A compiled volume states several (2 of 185 published transcripts, 2026-10-03; CHRG-117shrg56721 states eleven) and this is the first: it dates the package, as date_issued does, so there it is when the series began, not each session's date.  hearing_bill_links.held_date is NULL on the same volume for a different reason: a link pairs a date with a bill, and the volume pairs none.
columns.mods_event_id: The committee-meeting event id the package's GovInfo MODS states in `<eventId>` (the first, where it states several), which committee_meetings.event_id joins on with congress and chamber.  A second publisher's statement beside event_id, never overriding it: a consumer may fall back to it where event_id is NULL.  43 of 185 published transcripts state one, 22 where Congress.gov names none, 21 of them Senate; where both state one they agree 21 of 21 (2026-10-03), including a misassignment both make (CHRG-118hhrg63377 names 116369, another subcommittee's hearing that day), so agreement is not independent confirmation.

columns.package_id: The GovInfo package id; package_id and last_modified identify this retained revision.
columns.congress: The numbered Congress, as the keyed summary states it: the Congress the report was *filed* in.  For a Senate report that is the Congress after the one it covers; `covered_congress` is the one its printed bills belong to.
columns.session: The session of Congress the summary states.
columns.title: The package title as the keyed summary states it.
columns.date_issued: The date the package was issued.
columns.last_modified: The publisher's package addition/update timestamp, including metadata-only updates. Together with package_id it identifies a retained revision; it is not first publication or a promise that every text change has a unique timestamp.
columns.committee_system_code: The `authorityId` of the first `congCommittee` the MODS names: the committee whose activity this report is, already keyed the way `committees.system_code` is.  Never read off the printed cover, which the citation rules read for a different purpose.
columns.committee_name: That committee's `authority-standard` name, as the MODS spells it.
columns.submitted_by_bioguide_id: The `bioGuideId` of the member the MODS names with `role="SUBMITTEDBY"`.  The one bioguide id any of these documents states -- the citation rules measured zero *printed* ones across ten families -- and NULL where the publisher states the member without an id, which CRPT-118hrpt965 does.
columns.committee_count: How many committees the MODS names; every one is in committees.
columns.committees: Every `congCommittee` the MODS names, as a Native list of objects carrying the authority id, chamber, name and the Congress the authority record itself states -- which is the roster's Congress and not necessarily this report's. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.associated_bill_count: How many bills the MODS names; every one is in associated_bills.
columns.associated_bills: Every root-level `<bill>` the MODS names, as a Native list of objects carrying the bill's natural key and the publisher's own `context` marker, in document order.  The context is kept because document order is not priority order. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.associated_law_count: How many laws the MODS names; every one is in associated_laws.
columns.associated_laws: Every root-level `<law>` the MODS names, as a Native list of joined `laws` identities, in document order.  Carried because it is what the beyond-index bill and law counts are measured against. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.associated_usc_section_count: How many U.S. Code sections the MODS names; every one is in associated_usc_sections.
columns.associated_usc_sections: Every `<USCode>` *section* the MODS names, as a Native list of objects carrying the `{title}-{section}` key and the publisher's own subsection detail, in document order.  A chapter-only `<USCode>` block contributes nothing: a chapter is not a section and has no hosted key. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.related_report_count: How many sibling reports the MODS names; every one is in related_reports.
columns.related_reports: Every `<congReport>` the MODS names, as a Native list of CRPT package ids, in document order: the report-to-report edge, stated by the publisher rather than read off the print. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.distinct_bills: How many distinct bill keys the print names, by the shared citation rules.  A floor, not a total: it counts what pages_read reached, and the MODS is the authoritative list.  A key carries `covered_congress`, because a print mostly writes `H.R. 7806` with no Congress beside it, unless the print states the bill's own: set right after it (`H.R. 6752, 115th Cong.`), else in a Congress subheading over it (`116th Congress`), which it takes instead; where the report states none, these are the printed forms, unresolved.
columns.distinct_bills_beyond_index: How many of those the MODS does not already state, which is a measured floor and not a discovery rate: 0 of 1,406 across all eight sampled reports at full page depth.  The per-row `document_citations.stated_by_index` carries the same comparison exactly; this column is its summary for one document.  NULL where `covered_congress` is, because a printed bill without a Congress cannot be compared with the MODS's keys.
columns.bills_congress_mismatch: How many printed bills the MODS states under a *different* Congress than `covered_congress`: the same comparison run a second time on `(bill_type, number)` alone.  Nonzero on a Senate report is the publisher's index disagreeing with the report -- GovInfo stamps a Senate report's `<bill>` list with the filing Congress, so CRPT-118srpt99's H.R. 5376 is `118` in its MODS and `117` in its print, which reports on the 117th.  Nonzero on a House report counts the bills the print keys in an earlier Congress -- beside the bill or in a subheading over it -- which the MODS stamps with the filing one, and any measure of another Congress the print names without saying so, whose row's `bill_id` is then wrong.  NULL where `covered_congress` is.
columns.distinct_laws: How many distinct public laws the print names; a floor bounded by pages_read.
columns.distinct_laws_beyond_index: How many of those the MODS does not already state: 0 of 174 across all eight sampled reports at full page depth.  A floor with `stated_by_index` semantics, not a yield estimate.
columns.distinct_usc_sections: How many distinct U.S. Code sections the print names; a floor bounded by pages_read.
columns.distinct_usc_sections_beyond_index: How many of those the MODS does not already state: 0 of 37 across all eight sampled reports at full page depth.  This is the correction that removed U.S. Code sections from the family's claimed new yield; the kinds that survive are committees, RINs, agency dockets and GAO ids.
columns.citation_rows: How many citation rows this document produced, across every kind.
columns.stated_page_count: How many pages the document has, as the keyed summary's own `pages` field states it -- not re-derived from the bytes.  Named apart from `committee_reports.page_count`, which is a package-keyed column holding how many pages *that* extraction read: the two would otherwise collide on one `package_id` with opposite meanings (282 against 60 on CRPT-118hrpt965).
columns.body_version_id: Digest of the normalized text the citation spans index into.
columns.covered_congress: The Congress the report says it reports on, read from its own words -- the index title, else the print's cover, else its first five pages, and `covered_congress_source` says which -- and the Congress a printed bill key is built in where the print states no other for it.  Beside `congress` rather than replacing it: the two differ on every Senate report, which is filed early in the following Congress (CRPT-118srpt99 reports on the 117th).  NULL where the report states no Congress, or where the first source stating one states several; its printed bills the print states no Congress for then stay unresolved rather than being stamped with a guess.

columns.communication_id: Natural key: congress, lowercase communication type and number joined with hyphens.
columns.congress: The numbered Congress the communication was received in.
columns.communication_type: The publisher's communication type code, lowercased the way its own address spells it (ec, ml, ...).
columns.communication_type_name: The publisher's name for that type (Executive Communication, Memorial, ...).
columns.number: The communication's number within its Congress and type.
columns.chamber: The chamber, as the publisher spells it.
columns.session: The session of Congress the communication was received in.
columns.abstract: The publisher's abstract: the Record's own description of the communication. On a `congressional-record-granule` row it is the printed entry under the four normalizations the publisher's own abstract applies, which `record_entry_text` keeps unapplied.
columns.report_nature: The nature of the report transmitted, where the detail states one; where the RIN is read from.
columns.legal_authority: The statutory authority the communication cites, where the detail states one; a Congressional Review Act rule submission cites 5 U.S.C. 801(a)(1)(A).
columns.submitting_agency: The agency that submitted the communication, where the detail states one.
columns.submitting_official: The official who submitted it, where the detail states one.
columns.congressional_record_date: The date the communication appeared in the Congressional Record.
columns.is_rulemaking: Whether the publisher flags the communication as a rulemaking: the publisher's `True`/`False` strings folded onto the one published truth spelling; any other spelling refuses.
columns.referral_system_code: System code of the first committee the communication was referred to. NULL on a `congressional-record-granule` row: the Record prints a name, and the resolver from a name to a `committees.system_code` is not built.
columns.referral_committee_name: That committee's name as the publisher spells it; on a `congressional-record-granule` row, as the Record printed it, which is the committee's name on the day and agrees with Congress.gov's current spelling on 71.5% of held-out rows. Resolve identity through `referral_system_code`, never through this.
columns.referral_count: How many committees the detail lists; every one is in committees, and NULL where it is NULL.
columns.committees: Every committee referral the detail lists, as a Native list of the publisher's objects. NULL where no detail was read or the detail states no committees; `[]` where it states an empty list. On a `congressional-record-granule` row, one `{name}` object per committee the printed referral tail names, in printed order. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.matching_requirement_number: Number of the first House reporting requirement the communication matches.
columns.matching_requirement_count: How many requirements the detail lists; every one is in matching_requirements, and NULL where it is NULL.
columns.matching_requirements: Every matching requirement the detail lists, as a Native list of numbers. NULL where no detail was read or the detail states no such list; `[]` where it states an empty one. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.rin: The Regulation Identifier Number read from report_nature, where the rule found one: the first occurrence in rin_occurrences_json that a RIN label directly precedes, as its published key.
columns.rins: All interpreted RIN occurrences supplied by the consumer, with exact field spans and digest. NULL means unread; [] means the supplied field was read and contained no RIN. Each occurrence's field_sha256 is spelled sha256: plus the hex digest under the rule report_nature/shared_rin/2; one stored under the earlier report_nature/shared_rin carries the bare hex and is re-read, not reused. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.update_date: The publisher's updateDate; the merge prefers the larger value, except across source_route, where a `congress-gov-detail` row always wins.
columns.source_route: What produced this row: `congress-gov-detail` where the publisher decomposed the communication itself, `congressional-record-granule` where it was reconstructed from the printed entry.
columns.record_package_id: The exact Congressional Record package that printed the communication. May also be filled on a Congress.gov API row from a unique captured entry with matching Congress, communication type and number. Missing, ambiguous or incomplete reads leave it empty.
columns.record_granule_id: The exact House executive-communications granule that printed the entry. Paired with record_package_id; repeated qualifying entries do not supply a scalar locator.
columns.record_entry_text: The entry's printed text, retained beside the original Congress.gov fields. An API row keeps its original abstract, report nature and source route when this field is filled.

columns.congress: The Congress the table page states in its caption.
columns.session: The session (1 or 2) the table page states in its caption.
columns.seq: Zero-based position of this line in the page; part of the identity because one line can repeat.
columns.law_id: Natural key of the law, as laws keys it.
columns.law_number: The public law number as the table prints it, Congress prefix included.
columns.law_type: Always `public`: the page is the publisher's table for public laws.
columns.number: The law's number within its Congress.
columns.usc_title: The U.S. Code title as printed; a trailing A means the title's appendix, per the page's legend.
columns.usc_section: The U.S. Code section as printed.
columns.action: Column 3 verbatim; NULL where the page left it blank. The page's own legend (Explanation of Table, column 3, as the retained tbl119pl_2nd.htm prints it): `nt` means note; `nt [tbl]` means note [table]; `prec` means preceding; `fr` means a transfer from another section; `to` means a transfer to another section; `new` means a new section or new note; `gen amd` means the section or note is generally amended; `omitted` means the section is omitted; `repealed` means the section or note is repealed; `nt ed chg` and `ed chg` refer to the Editorial Classification Change Table; no entry or `nt` by itself means the section or note is amended. Tokens combine (`nt new`: a new note). A transfer prints as `tr fr <title>/<section>` (from that section) or `tr to <title>/<section>` (to it), the legend's `fr` and `to`. The leading `nt` or `prec` is the row's place, which usc_place states.
columns.act_section: The law's own section that did it, as printed; a quoted item after it names a new section.
columns.statutes_at_large_volume: The volume the page's column header names.
columns.statutes_at_large_page: The page as printed: one page, or a span such as two pages joined by a comma or a dash.
columns.link_volume: The volume in the row's statviewer link, where the row carries one.
columns.link_page: The page in the row's statviewer link, where the row carries one.
columns.table_order: Which of the publisher's two orders the page is: `public-law` or `code`; both hold the same lines.
columns.stated_laws: The law range the page's caption states it covers, verbatim.
columns.prepared_date: The date the page states it was prepared.
columns.usc_section_key: The one U.S. Code section the row names, as a join key: the section number without Table III's printed note words (`nt`, `nts`, `prec.`; usc_place states them), lower-cased, with every dash spelling an ASCII hyphen, as RefSpec's section oracle keys it. Both OLRC tables key it the same way, so they meet on usc_title, usc_section_key and usc_place; without usc_place a note line meets the section's own line. Fold another source the same way (schemas.tables.usc_section_key): document_citations' usc_section rule 001 keeps the printed case and dashes. NULL where usc_section is NULL or names no single section (a list, a range or a chapter, which Table III prints for some older acts), and on rows published before the column existed.
columns.usc_place: Where on that section the row lands: `section` (the section itself), `note` (a note under it; OLRC's `nt` or `nts`), `preceding` (the place just before it, such as a chapter or subchapter heading a law adds there; `prec`) or `note_preceding` (a note at that place). Read from the section as Table III prints it (`1101 nt`, `prec. 1071`, `nt. prec. 791`) and from the head of law_code_sections.action (`nt new`, `prec`, `nt prec new`), by schemas.law_tables.usc_section_place. NULL where usc_section_key is NULL, and on rows published before the column existed.

columns.law_id: Validated congress-kind-number law key; joins laws.law_id and through laws.bill_id to the enacted measure.
columns.seq: Zero-based native section occurrence in document order; missing or repeated labels never merge rows.
columns.publisher_id: The section element's literal id attribute, including repeats; NULL if missing.
columns.publisher_identifier: The section element's literal identifier attribute, not inferred from its number.
columns.section_number: Text of the section's direct num element; repeated direct num elements are newline-joined and flagged.
columns.section_number_value: The single direct num element's value attribute, where stated; NULL for missing or repeated num elements.
columns.heading: Mixed inline text of the direct heading; repeated direct headings are newline-joined and flagged.
columns.parent_seq: Occurrence of the nearest containing native section; NULL for sections without a section ancestor.
columns.hierarchy: Source-order structural ancestors with element, namespace-qualified path, native IDs, number and heading. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.body: Section-owned source text: block boundaries become newlines; inline adjacency survives, amending actions included. Excludes own number/heading, print furniture and nested sections, which have separate rows. Print furniture is the page's apparatus beside the enacted words: page numbers, running heads and, from law_text_reader_version law-sections-uslm-v2, the USLM sidenote margin notes (`42 USC 405 note.`, a topical catchword such as `Contracts.`), each flagged in issues_json as print_furniture_excluded:<element>; under law-sections-uslm-v1 the margin notes were kept as body lines. This is not consolidated or applied law text.
columns.is_quoted: true when a native quotedContent ancestor encloses this section; a quoted section is not a separate enacted section.

columns.law_id: Natural key: congress, law_type and number joined with hyphens.
columns.congress: The numbered Congress that enacted the law.
columns.law_type: `public` or `private`: the publisher's Public Law or Private Law folded onto the spelling the PLAW USLM publicPrivate field uses, so the list route, the bulk folder and the USLM file share one key.
columns.number: The law's number within its Congress and type, without the Congress prefix.
columns.law_number: The publisher's own spelling of the number, Congress prefix included.
columns.publisher_law_type: The publisher's laws[].type exactly as spelled (Public Law or Private Law).
columns.package_id: The GovInfo PLAW package id by the measured bulk-file rule: `PLAW-` plus congress, publ or pvtl, and number.
columns.bill_id: Natural key of the measure this law enacted, as congress_bills keys it.
columns.bill_type: The enacted measure's type, lowercased as the bill tables spell it.
columns.title: The measure's title as the list route states it.
columns.origin_chamber: The chamber the measure originated in, as the publisher states it.
columns.origin_chamber_code: The publisher's one-letter origin chamber code.
columns.latest_action_date: Date of the publisher's latestAction entry. Usually the became-law action, but the publisher lists a later action when there is one (119-public-68: a committee report filed after signing), so for the enactment date read approved_date where the PLAW was captured, else congress_bills.signed_date through bill_id (a private law's too).
columns.update_date: The publisher's updateDate on the list row; the merge prefers the larger value.
columns.update_date_including_text: The publisher's updateDateIncludingText on the list row.
columns.statutes_at_large_cite: The native Statutes at Large citation, when stated. NULL with captured_partial means the acquired identity-matched USLM does not state this citation; see uslm_reason and uslm_citable_as.
columns.statutes_at_large_volume: The volume part of that citation.
columns.statutes_at_large_page: The page part of that citation.
columns.approved_date: The USLM meta's approvedDate, where the PLAW was captured.
columns.uslm_title: The USLM meta's dc:title, where the PLAW was captured.
columns.uslm_outcome: captured or captured_partial retain validated native metadata; captured_refused retains a refused capture without unvalidated metadata; request_failed records an attempted read without an accepted body; unavailable records supported source absence; not_requested means no attempt.
columns.uslm_citable_as: Every literal native USLM meta citableAs value, source order retained. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.uslm_reason: Bounded outcome reason token; NULL on complete capture or when no read was attempted.
columns.law_text_outcome: not_requested, parsed or refused: section reading is separate from validated USLM metadata.
columns.law_section_count: Native section occurrences emitted by a successful read, including quoted nested sections; NULL unless parsed.
columns.law_body_remainder: Main-body text outside every native section subtree, including hierarchy headings and enacting formula; block-spaced like section body. Empty string means parsed with no remainder; NULL means not parsed. Print furniture (page numbers, running heads and, from law_text_reader_version law-sections-uslm-v2, the margin notes: the approval date, the bill number, the short-title note) is excluded with an issue in law_text_issues_json.
columns.law_text_url: Actual resolved XML acquisition URL for an attempted law-text read, distinct from the bill API url. Supplied from capture evidence, never inferred; NULL when unattempted or the caller retained no URL. A refused read does not validate the target's law identity.
columns.statutes_at_large_last_page: The last Statutes at Large page the law is printed on: the last page marker the PLAW USLM states in the cited volume (`<page identifier="/us/stat/140/746">`), so a page from statutes_at_large_page to this one, in statutes_at_large_volume, is inside the law. On the 102 public laws of the 119th's PLAW file (2026-09-14) the first marker is the cited page on every law and the next law starts on the following page on 97 of 98 consecutive pairs (one page between on the other). NULL where no USLM was captured, it states no citation or no marker in its volume, and on a row read under uslm_reader_version laws-uslm-v2 or earlier.

columns.lifecycle_event_id: Stable identity of this lifecycle event within its lifecycle.
columns.document_id: The document, by `dated_by`: a dated Register record id (`number@YYYY-MM-DD`), a Regulations.gov document id, or an agenda item id (`urn:rkaf:us:rin:<rin>`).
columns.stage: The stage the event records: `proposed`, `supplemental`, `final` or `withdrawn`.
columns.event_date: The event's day, from the source `dated_by` names.
columns.document_form: Its stage refined by its title: `proposed`, `advance_proposed`, `comment_period`, `final`, `interim_final`, `direct_final`, `correction`, `supplemental` or `withdrawn`.
columns.anchor_role: `proposal`, `final` or `withdrawal` when the lifecycle anchors on this document; NULL otherwise.
columns.source: Who typed the stage: `federal_register` (for its copies too, wherever it states a type), `regulations_gov` or `unified_agenda`.
columns.dated_by: Whose day `event_date` is, and so which kind of id `document_id` is: `federal_register`, `regulations_gov` (its upload) or `unified_agenda`.
columns.evidence_id: The proceedings stage event it came from: that record's own id, or `<agenda item id>@<edition>` for an Agenda withdrawal.
columns.joined_by: How the document joined the proceeding: `docket`, `fr_docket_link`, `fr_copy`, `specific_rin` or `agenda_rin`.

columns.filing_uuid: The filing this activity belongs to; joins to `lobbying_filings.filing_uuid`.
columns.activity_index: The activity's position in the filing's list, from `0`. With `filing_uuid`, the key.
columns.description: The registrant's description of the specific lobbying, often naming bills (e.g. `S. 3597`).
columns.foreign_entity_issues: The registrant's statement of any foreign entity's interest in the issue; often null.
columns.government_entities: Native list of the government entities contacted for this activity, `{id, name}` objects (e.g. `SENATE`). Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.

columns.activity_index: The activity's position in the filing; with `filing_uuid`, joins to `lobbying_activities`.
columns.lobbyist_index: The lobbyist's position in the activity's list, from `0`. Completes the key.
columns.lobbyist_id: LDA's lobbyist record id: one registrant's record of a lobbyist, stable across that registrant's filings, not an identity for the person. LDA's own record for an id (`lda.gov/api/v1/lobbyists/<id>/`) names exactly one registrant, so a lobbyist who moves to another firm is filed under a new id: Stephen Holland is 146616 under registrant 11377 and 151303 under registrant 7257. A count of distinct ids counts registrant-lobbyist records, not people; matching a person across firms is a name match. A few ids also appear on another registrant's filing, all on filings of 2020-2022 (measured 2026-10-03).
columns.prefix: Name prefix as filed; often null.
columns.first_name: First name as filed (LDA prints names upper-case).
columns.middle_name: Middle name as filed; often null.
columns.suffix: Name suffix as filed; often null.
columns.covered_position: The covered executive- or legislative-branch position the lobbyist held, as the registrant typed it for this activity: free text, not parsed, with no link to `committees` or any agency table. It is stated per activity, so one lobbyist's rows can carry it on some activities and not others; NULL means this entry states none, not that the lobbyist held none. Many values are placeholders rather than positions (`N/A`, `None`, `Not applicable`) or point elsewhere (`See prior filing`), and LDA's own filings sometimes put a colleague's text against the wrong name.
columns.new: `True` when the filing lists the lobbyist as new for this activity, `False` otherwise.

columns.filing_uuid: LDA filing UUID (e.g. `7866327b-c892-4430-b9f0-1f0f679c58c6`). Primary key / dedup key.
columns.filing_type: The LDA filing-type code as the API states it: `RR` registration; `Q1`–`Q4` quarterly reports and `MM` the pre-2008 mid-year report; `1A`–`4A` and `MA` amendments; `1T`–`4T` and `MT` terminations; `1@`–`4@` and `M@` termination amendments; a trailing `Y` marks a no-activity report (`Q1Y`, `1@Y`). The LDA constants endpoint (`/api/v1/constants/filing/filingtypes/`) is the authority. An amendment is a separate filing that restates its quarter's report. To total amounts, drop registrations (`RR`, `RA`), which carry a `filing_period` too, then keep the latest filing per registrant, `client_id` and period: with registrations kept, a later one displaced a quarterly report in 103 groups of 2025 (measured 2026-10-03). For issues or activities, choose filing types first: a termination chain (`1T`, then a no-activity `1@Y`) shares the period, and the latest filing can be the no-activity one.
columns.filing_year: Calendar year the filing reports on.
columns.dt_posted: Timestamp the filing was posted to the LDA system (ISO 8601 string with timezone). Sort key.
columns.registrant_name: Name of the registrant (the lobbying firm or self-filing organization).
columns.registrant_id: LDA registrant id. Stable join key across a registrant's filings.
columns.client_name: The client's name as the registrant filed it; a name, not an identity. A self-filing organization is both registrant and client, often under a spelling other registrants do not use for it (McKesson files as `MCKESSON CORPORATION & AFFILIATES …`). `registrant_id` keys the registrant across its filings and `client_id` keys a client only within one registrant (see `client_id`); a match to `comments.organization` or `sam_entities.legal_business_name` is a name match.
columns.client_id: LDA's `client.id`: one registrant's record of one client, stable across that registrant's filings, not an organization identity. No id is shared between registrants (129,434 ids for 129,434 registrant-client pairs, measured 2026-10-03), so an organization hired by several firms has one id per firm (AT&T Services, Inc.: 21 ids under 21 registrants in 2025).
columns.income: Lobbying income reported by a lobbying firm for the period, in USD. Null for self-filers (who report `expenses`). An amended report (`filing_type` `1A`–`4A`) restates its quarter's amount, often unchanged, so summing over every filing counts that quarter twice; drop registrations (`RR`, `RA`) and keep the latest filing per registrant, `client_id` and quarter (see `filing_type`).
columns.expenses: Lobbying expenses reported by a self-filing organization for the period, in USD. Null for firms (who report `income`). An amended report (`filing_type` `1A`–`4A`) restates its quarter's amount, often unchanged, so summing over every filing counts that quarter twice; drop registrations (`RR`, `RA`) and keep the latest filing per registrant, `client_id` and quarter (see `filing_type`). A self-filing organization's expenses already include what it pays outside lobbying firms, whose `income` for that client is reported separately; do not add the two.
columns.lobbying_activities: Native list of lobbying activities, each `{general_issue_code, general_issue_code_display, description}` — the issue areas lobbied and their free-text descriptions. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.government_entities: Government entities named on the filing, in order of first appearance. A rebuilt filing lists each source ID once and uses the source name when the ID is absent. The activity rows retain every occurrence. Earlier native generations may repeat entities at filing level. A missing activity list yields null and an empty activity list yields an empty result.
columns.filing_type_display: The publisher's label for `filing_type`, as served (e.g. `1st Quarter - Report`, `Registration`).
columns.filing_period_display: The publisher's label for `filing_period`, as served (e.g. `1st Quarter (Jan 1 - Mar 31)`).
columns.filing_document_content_type: Media type of the filing document at `url`, as LDA states it (e.g. `text/html`, `application/pdf`); null on the few filings that state none.
columns.expenses_method: The self-filer's expense accounting method code as filed (`expenses_method`). Two spellings occur, both kept as filed: lower case `a`, `b`, `c`, whose `expenses_method_display` is the long label, and upper case `A`, `B`, `C`, whose display is the bare letter; both occur in current years (a 400-page retained sample, 2026-10-30, held 751 lower-case and 286 upper-case codes). `a`/`A` is Method A (LDA definitions), `b`/`B` Method B (IRC 6033(b)(8)), `c`/`C` Method C (IRC 162(e)). Null when the filing states no method, as on most firm reports, which carry `income` instead.
columns.expenses_method_display: The publisher's label for `expenses_method`, as filed: `Method A - Reporting amounts using LDA definitions only`, `Method B - Reporting amounts under section 6033(b)(8) of the Internal Revenue Code`, `Method C - Reporting amounts under section 162(e) of the Internal Revenue Code`, or the bare letter when the code is upper case.
columns.termination_date: Date the registrant ended its representation of the client, on a termination report (`filing_type` `1T`–`4T`, `MT` and their no-activity forms). Null on other filings.
columns.posted_by_name: Name of the person who signed and posted the filing, as entered (often with a title, e.g. `Frank J. Donatelli, Senior Advisor`).
columns.registrant_address_1: First line of the registrant's address as filed on this filing. The address can differ between a registrant's filings; it is the filing's own, not a current registrant profile.
columns.registrant_address_2: Second line of the registrant's address as filed on this filing; null when none was filed.
columns.registrant_city: City of the registrant's address as filed on this filing.
columns.registrant_state: State code of the registrant's address as filed on this filing (e.g. `DC`); null for an address outside the United States.
columns.registrant_zip: ZIP or postal code of the registrant's address as filed on this filing.
columns.registrant_country: Country of the registrant's address as filed on this filing, as the publisher displays it (e.g. `United States of America`), not a country code.
columns.registrant_ppb_country: Country of the registrant's principal place of business as filed, when the filing states one (display name); null otherwise.
columns.registrant_different_address: The filing's flag for whether the registrant's principal place of business differs from the address filed: true, false, or null when the filing does not carry it (registrations among others).

columns.affiliation_index: Zero-based affiliation position within the source term.
columns.party: Literal nested party; NULL is not filled from the term-level party.
columns.affiliation_start: Literal nested start date; interval boundary policy belongs to the consumer.
columns.affiliation_end: Literal nested end date; a missing end does not imply an open interval.
columns.term_party: The separate term-level party assertion, not a dated fallback.
columns.caucus: Complete affiliation object, retaining absent, null and unknown fields. This column retains the source property caucus.

columns.bioguide_id: The legislator who served this term.
columns.term_index: Zero-based position in the crosswalk's own terms list; part of the identity.
columns.term_type: Chamber of this term: rep or sen.
columns.term_end: End date of this term, where the crosswalk states one.
columns.term_state: State this term was served for.
columns.term_party: The separate source term-level party assertion, not a dated history.
columns.term_district: District for this term, spelled as the publisher does; absent for a Senate term.

columns.member_key: The member's key within the roll call, as in `member_votes`.
columns.bioguide_id: The member's Bioguide id, as `member_votes` carries it: stated by the Clerk for the House from 2003, and resolved at the votes merge from the LIS id for the Senate and from the Clerk's printed label for a House row of 1990-2002. NULL when the LIS id or the label resolves to no one member; a `name:` key is never read as a person.
columns.vote_day: The vote's day (YYYY-MM-DD) as the chamber printed it in Eastern time, read from `member_votes.vote_date` by the same rule as `roll_call_votes.vote_day`; NULL when the file prints no date.
columns.term_match: `half_open` (one term with start <= day < end), `inclusive_end` (none half-open, exactly one with the end day included), `ambiguous` (more than one term either way), `unmatched` (none), `unresolved_member`, or `undated` (the file prints no date, so no term is chosen). `undated` wins over `unresolved_member`; such a row still carries `bioguide_id` wherever the member resolves.
columns.term_index: The matched term's `term_index` in `member_terms`; NULL unless matched.
columns.term_start: The matched term's start date; NULL unless matched.
columns.term_end: The matched term's end date; NULL unless matched.

columns.vote_id: The roll call this position belongs to, as roll_call_votes keys it.
columns.congress: The numbered Congress the roll call belongs to.
columns.session: The session number within that Congress.
columns.roll_number: The roll-call number within that session.
columns.member_key: The file-stated id: `lis:` plus the LIS id on a Senate record, the bare bioguide id on a House one, and `name:` plus the publisher's name where the file states neither (every Clerk file of 1990-2002). A Senate bioguide comes from the crosswalk and does not always resolve, so keying on it would split one member's votes across two rows; an identity column also cannot be null, which the design's bioguide key would have been. A `name:` key identifies the row within its roll call, not a person: across 1990-2002 at least 21 of the Clerk's labels name two different members (Jones (NC), Allen, Schiff, Wilson, McHugh, Smith (WA)...), so a person is the host's crosswalk, never this key. Congress, member_name, party and state do not identify one either: one Congress can seat a successor of the same surname, party and state (where the Clerk states bioguide ids, 5 such keys name two: 109th Matsui D-CA, 110th Carson D-IN, 112th Payne D-NJ, 117th Letlow R-LA, 119th Grijalva D-AZ; in 1990-2002 the 105th's Capps and Bono (CA) and the 107th's Shuster (PA) show it as a gap inside the Congress), so the crosswalk adds vote_date, checked against each member's service dates.
columns.bioguide_id: The voting member's bioguide id: stated by the publisher on a House row (the Clerk's name-id, from 2003), and filled by the host's crosswalk at merge time on a Senate row, whose file states only lis_id (members.lis_id resolves it); NULL where neither supplies one.
columns.lis_id: The voting member's Senate LIS id, which only the Senate file carries.
columns.member_name: The member's name exactly as the roll-call source spells it.
columns.party: The member's party as the roll-call source states it.
columns.state: The member's state as the roll-call source states it. On a House row `XX` is the Clerk's marking for the non-voting delegates and the Resident Commissioner, on the roll calls they voted in: 2,169 of the Clerk's 22,512 of 1990-2026 (1993-1994, 2007-2010, 2019-2020 and from 2022; none in 2021), every one an amendment vote or a motion in committee (to rise, to strike or limit debate, a call in committee, a ruling of the chair), filed under <committee> (clerk_body_element on roll_call_votes) from 2007 and under <chamber> in 1993-1994.  Kept as stated, not mapped to a territory.
columns.position: The member's position exactly as the publisher spelled it (Yea, Aye, Not Voting...).
columns.position_normalized: That position folded onto yea, nay, present or not_voting; NULL for a named candidate choice.
columns.vote_date: The chamber's literal date; sorts as text, not by time (see roll_call_votes `vote_day`).

columns.bioguide_id: The Biographical Directory id, which is this crosswalk's primary identifier.
columns.bioguide_previous: The source list of previous Bioguide ids in its order, as JSON; absent is NULL. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.lis_id: The Senate LIS id, which only senators carry.
columns.fec_ids: Every FEC candidate id for this person, as a Native list in the publisher's order. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.icpsr_id: The ICPSR id used by roll-call research datasets.
columns.votesmart_id: The Vote Smart person id from the community crosswalk; absent when unstated.
columns.name_first: The person's first name as the crosswalk spells it.
columns.name_last: The person's last name as the crosswalk spells it.
columns.other_names: Source other_names patches in order, with literal date bounds and nulls; absent is NULL. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.term_count: How many terms the crosswalk lists; the member_terms row count for this person.
columns.first_term_start: Start date of the earliest term listed.
columns.last_term_end: End date of the latest term listed.
columns.current_term_type: Chamber of the latest term: rep or sen.
columns.current_term_party: Party of the latest term, as the crosswalk states it for that term.
columns.current_term_district: District of the latest term; absent for a Senate term.
columns.name_nickname: The crosswalk's own name.nickname for the person, as it spells it; NULL means the crosswalk states none, not that the person has none.
columns.name_middle: The crosswalk's own name.middle for the person, as it spells it; NULL means the crosswalk states none, not that the person has none.
columns.name_suffix: The crosswalk's own name.suffix for the person, as it spells it; NULL means the crosswalk states none, not that the person has none.
columns.name_official_full: The crosswalk's own name.official_full for the person, as it spells it; NULL means the crosswalk states none, not that the person has none.

columns.scope_id: The input's replacement scope, `native_reference_scope_id` over source_family, source_record_key and edition; a complete read replaces every row of its scope, and a successful empty read clears it.
columns.source_family: The scanner family that read the input: `uscode`, `ecfr`, `bill` or `law`, fixed by the shaper.
columns.source_record_key: The caller's record identity for the input, retained literally.
columns.edition: The edition or request date the caller's checked capture metadata states, literally; NULL when it states none, never read from a filename.
columns.body_version_id: `sha256:` digest of the exact retained XML bytes the scanner read.
columns.source_locator: Where the caller retained the input from, literally; not proof of acquisition time or edition.
columns.occurrence_index: The observation's zero-based position among the input's observations, both kinds counted together in the order the scanner reported them, as decimal text.
columns.source_path: The observed element's positional XPath in the input (`/*[1]/*[2]`), never a byte offset.
columns.element_tag: The observed element's tag, its namespace expanded (`{http://xml.house.gov/schemas/uslm/1.0}ref`) where the input declares one.
columns.observation_kind: `native_reference` for a bill or law observation, `native_reference` or `source_credit` for a U.S. Code observation, `authority` (AUTH) or `source_note` (SOURCE) for an eCFR note.
columns.href: The element's href exactly as stated, an empty string when stated empty; NULL when absent, and on every source credit and note.
columns.text: The complete decoded text of a source credit or note, whitespace kept; NULL on a native reference.
columns.text_runs: An eCFR note's text split at element boundaries, as a Native list whose strings join to text; NULL on U.S. Code rows. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.cfr_title: The CFR title the caller's checked capture metadata states, on an eCFR note; NULL when it states none, never inferred from a fragment.
columns.cfr_part: The `N` of the nearest enclosing DIV5 part on an eCFR note; NULL when no part encloses it, and on U.S. Code rows.
columns.interpretation_status: How the reading under rule_version read this observation: `native_section_href`, `native_statute_href`, `native_public_law_href` or `unsupported_href` for an href, `native_bill_usc_cite` for a qualified bill DTD cite, `partial_text_findings` or `no_qualified_text_findings` for text; it does not claim exhaustive extraction.
columns.target_candidates: The typed targets the reading found, as a Native list in reading order, each with the outcome of the host's lookup in the target tables it selected; several targets in one note stay one row, and an unsupported href has none. Stored as native nested values; list order, repeated values, null and empty collections remain distinct.
columns.rule_version: `native-legal-reference/003` (`NATIVE_LEGAL_REFERENCE_RULE`): the scanners' selected shapes and the reading this row was produced under, comparable for equality only.
columns.native_element_id: Publisher element identifier attached to this legal reference.
columns.native_idref: Publisher identifier reference attached to this legal reference.
columns.native_class: Publisher classification attached to this legal reference.

columns.nomination_id: Canonical nomination key ({congress}-pn-{number}, plus -{part} when part_number is non-zero).
columns.citation: The publisher's citation, its own display key, with the part where one exists (PN730-20).
columns.congress: The numbered Congress the nomination was received in.
columns.part_number: The part number, as the publisher spells it.
columns.description: The publisher's description of the nomination.
columns.organization: The organization the nominee would serve in.
columns.received_date: The date the Senate received the nomination.
columns.is_civilian: Whether the nomination is civilian, as the publisher's nominationType states it: `true` where it states isCivilian true (or isMilitary false), `false` where it states isMilitary true (or isCivilian false). The list route states exactly one of the two keys (2,287 of 2,287 rows of the 119th, 2026-10-03). NULL where it states neither, or both with contradicting values; nomination_type_json keeps what it stated, so `is_civilian IS NULL AND nomination_type_json IS NOT NULL` counts the contradictions.
columns.is_military: The publisher's nominationType object, as JSON. This column retains the source property isMilitary.
columns.latest_action_date: Date of the publisher's latestAction entry.
